summary.en: On the desert pampa between Nazca and Palpa, the Nazca people swept aside dark surface stones to draw hundreds of straight lines, trapezoids and giant figures of animals and plants, many visible as wholes only from the air. Their purpose, probably ritual walking and water cults, is still debated.
summary.zh: 在纳斯卡与帕尔帕之间的荒原上，纳斯卡人清除地表深色石块，绘出数百条直线、梯形以及巨大的动植物图形，许多图案只有从空中才能看到全貌。其用途可能与仪式行走和祈水崇拜有关，至今仍有争论。

story.en:
The lines are shallow: removing the iron-stained pebbles of the pampa exposes paler ground a few centimetres below, and the dry, windless climate has preserved them for some two thousand years. Most of the famous figures, among them the hummingbird, the monkey with a spiral tail and the spider, belong to the Nazca culture of roughly 100 BCE to 700 CE.

The Peruvian archaeologist Toribio Mejía Xesspe described them in 1927, and in 1941 the American historian Paul Kosok, watching the sun set along one line at the solstice, called the pampa the largest astronomy book in the world. The German mathematician Maria Reiche spent half a century mapping and guarding them.

Most researchers now link the lines to processions and to rituals for water in one of the driest places on Earth. Drones and machine learning keep adding to the count: in 2024 a team from Yamagata University reported more than 300 new small figures.
story.zh:
这些线条很浅：搬开荒原上被铁锈染色的卵石，下方几厘米处便露出颜色较浅的地面；干燥无风的气候让它们保存了约两千年。最著名的图形，如蜂鸟、尾巴卷曲的猴子和蜘蛛，大多属于约公元前100年至公元700年的纳斯卡文化。

1927年秘鲁考古学家托里维奥·梅希亚·谢斯佩首次记述了这些线条。1941年美国历史学家保罗·科索克在至日观看太阳沿一条直线落下，称这片荒原为“世界上最大的天文书”。德国数学家玛丽亚·赖歇用了半个世纪测绘和守护它们。

如今多数研究者认为，这些线条与游行仪式以及在地球上最干旱地区之一祈求水源的仪式有关。无人机和机器学习不断增加已知图形的数量：2024年日本山形大学团队报告发现了三百多个新的小型图案。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Lines and Geoglyphs of Nasca and Palpa
Britannica: Nazca Lines
Masato Sakai et al., “AI-accelerated Nazca survey nearly doubles the number of known figurative geoglyphs”, PNAS 121 (2024)

note: Construction spans roughly 500 BCE – 700 CE; the year 1 marks the Nazca period proper within the atlas range.

summary.en: In the upper Magdalena valley of southern Colombia, a people whose name is lost carved hundreds of stone figures, fanged guardians, eagles and double-selves, to stand over the burial mounds and stone tombs of their chiefs. The site is the largest group of megalithic sculpture in South America.
summary.zh: 在哥伦比亚南部马格达莱纳河上游河谷，一个已不知其名的民族雕刻了数百尊石像——獠牙守护者、鹰和“双身”形象——立于其首领的墓丘和石墓之上。这里是南美洲规模最大的巨石雕塑群。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: San Agustín Archaeological Park
Gerardo Reichel-Dolmatoff, San Agustín: A Culture of Colombia (Thames & Hudson, 1972)

note: The statues are dated mainly to the Regional Classic period, c. 1–900 CE.

summary.en: A stepped adobe pyramid of the Lima culture, built in the middle of what is now Lima’s Miraflores district. Its builders set small hand-made bricks upright like books on a shelf, a technique that helped the mound survive earthquakes; it served as a ceremonial and administrative centre.
summary.zh: 利马文化的阶梯状土坯金字塔，位于今利马米拉弗洛雷斯区中心。建造者把手制小砖像书架上的书一样竖立砌筑，这种技术使台丘得以抵御地震；它曾是礼仪与行政中心。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Huaca Pucllana
Isabel Flores Espinoza, Pucllana: esplendor de la cultura Lima (2005)

name.en: Royal tomb of the Lord of Sipán

summary.en: Around 250 CE a Moche warrior-priest was buried at Huaca Rajada near Sipán, dressed in gold and silver regalia and accompanied by sacrificed attendants. Found intact by Walter Alva in 1987, the tomb is the richest unlooted burial ever excavated in the Americas.
summary.zh: 约公元250年，一位莫切武士祭司被葬于西潘附近的瓦卡拉哈达，身着金银礼服，并有殉葬侍从相伴。1987年瓦尔特·阿尔瓦发现这座完好无损的墓葬，它是美洲迄今发掘的最豪华的未被盗掘墓葬。

story.en:
In February 1987 police in Lambayeque recovered gold objects from looters who had tunnelled into Huaca Rajada, a pair of eroded adobe pyramids near the village of Sipán. The archaeologist Walter Alva, director of the regional museum, moved onto the site to stop further digging, sometimes under armed guard.

In June his team reached an intact burial chamber. The lord lay in a wooden coffin, wearing gold and turquoise ear ornaments, necklaces of gold and silver peanuts, a crescent headdress and a backflap. Around him were a dog, two llamas, three young women, a child and men who may have been a warrior and a guard, one with his feet removed, perhaps so that he could never leave his post.

His regalia match the “Warrior Priest” painted on Moche pots, showing that the scenes depicted real rituals. The finds are displayed in the Royal Tombs of Sipán Museum, opened in Lambayeque in 2002.
story.zh:
1987年2月，兰巴耶克警方从盗墓者手中追回一批金器，盗墓者在西潘村附近两座风化的土坯金字塔瓦卡拉哈达中挖了地道。地区博物馆馆长、考古学家瓦尔特·阿尔瓦随即进驻遗址阻止盗掘，有时需要武装警卫保护。

同年6月，考古队找到一座完好的墓室。墓主躺在木棺中，戴着金与绿松石耳饰、金银花生串成的项链、新月形头冠和护背。周围有一条狗、两头羊驼、三名年轻女子、一个孩子，以及可能是武士和守卫的男子，其中一人双脚被截去，或许是为了让他永远不能离开岗位。

他的服饰与莫切陶器上描绘的“武士祭司”完全吻合，说明这些画面记录的是真实仪式。出土文物陈列于2002年在兰巴耶克开放的西潘王陵博物馆。

sources.title: Walter Alva & Christopher B. Donnan, Royal Tombs of Sipán (UCLA Fowler Museum, 1993)
Britannica: Moche
Wikipedia: Huaca Rajada

note: The burial is dated to c. 250 CE (± several decades).

name.en: Huacas del Sol y de la Luna

summary.en: The Moche capital in the Moche valley grew around two huge adobe platforms. Huaca del Sol, built from an estimated 140 million marked bricks, was the largest adobe structure in the Americas; the Huaca de la Luna temple was rebuilt in layers whose painted friezes of the decapitator god survive.
summary.zh: 莫切河谷的莫切首都围绕两座巨大的土坯平台发展。太阳神庙估计由约1.4亿块带标记的土砖砌成，是美洲最大的土坯建筑；月亮神庙则层层重建，其彩绘的“斩首神”浮雕保存至今。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Huacas del Sol y de la Luna
Steve Bourget & Kimberly L. Jones (eds.), The Art and Archaeology of the Moche (University of Texas Press, 2008)
Charles M. Hastings & M. Edward Moseley, “The Adobes of Huaca del Sol and Huaca de la Luna”, American Antiquity 40:2 (1975)

note: In 1602 Spanish treasure hunters diverted the Moche river to wash away part of the Huaca del Sol.

name.en: Burial of the Lady of Cao

summary.en: At the El Brujo complex a Moche woman in her twenties was buried around 450 CE with gold crowns, nose ornaments, war clubs and spear-throwers, her arms tattooed with snakes and spiders. Found in 2005, she showed that women could hold the highest political and religious power in Moche society.
summary.zh: 约公元450年，一位二十多岁的莫切女性被葬于埃尔布鲁霍遗址，随葬金冠、鼻饰、战棍和投矛器，双臂纹有蛇和蜘蛛图案。2005年她被发现，表明女性在莫切社会中可以掌握最高的政治与宗教权力。

story.en:
Archaeologists of the El Brujo project, led by Régulo Franco, were excavating the Huaca Cao Viejo pyramid in 2005 when they found a tomb sealed inside the adobe layers. Inside a cotton bundle lay a young woman, remarkably preserved by the salts and dry air, her skin still showing tattoos.

Her grave goods were those of a ruler: 44 gold and silver nose ornaments, crowns, needles and spindles alongside clubs and spear-throwers, symbols of military authority. A teenage girl, perhaps sacrificed, lay beside her. Until then Moche rulers had been assumed to be men.

She probably died after childbirth. A museum at El Brujo now displays her body, and a forensic reconstruction of her face was unveiled in 2017.
story.zh:
2005年，由雷古洛·佛朗哥领导的埃尔布鲁霍考古项目在发掘考老神庙金字塔时，发现一座封闭在土坯层中的墓葬。一个棉布包裹中躺着一位年轻女子，盐分和干燥空气使其保存得极为完好，皮肤上的纹身仍清晰可见。

她的随葬品属于统治者：44件金银鼻饰、王冠、针和纺锤，还有象征军事权威的战棍和投矛器。她身旁躺着一名可能被献祭的少女。在此之前，人们一直以为莫切统治者都是男性。

她很可能死于分娩之后。埃尔布鲁霍的博物馆现展出她的遗体，2017年还公布了法医复原的面容。

sources.title: Régulo Franco Jordán, La Señora de Cao (Fundación Wiese, 2009)
National Geographic, “Mummy of Tattooed Woman Shows Women Ruled in Moche Society” (2006)
Wikipedia: Lady of Cao

note: Dated by radiocarbon to around 450 CE.

name.zh: 马拉若岛的马拉若拉土丘文化

summary.en: On Marajó, the huge island at the mouth of the Amazon, people raised earth mounds (tesos) above the seasonal floods for villages and cemeteries and made elaborate painted and incised burial urns. Their society, which lasted about a millennium, overturned the idea that the Amazon could not support complex cultures.
summary.zh: 在亚马孙河口的巨岛马拉若上，人们堆筑高出季节性洪水的土丘（teso）作为村落和墓地，并制作精美的彩绘刻纹骨灰瓮。这一延续约千年的社会推翻了“亚马孙无法孕育复杂文化”的观点。

story.en:
Marajó floods for half the year, so its inhabitants built platforms of earth, some more than 10 metres high and covering several hectares. The largest groups of mounds, such as Camutins and Pacoval, held houses, hearths and cemeteries of urns painted in red, black and white with stylised human faces and serpents.

In the 1980s the American archaeologist Anna Roosevelt excavated Teso dos Bichos and argued that the mounds supported dense, chiefly societies feeding on fish and plant foods. Her conclusions were controversial, but later work by Denise Schaan and others confirmed a long-lived regional culture.

The tradition faded before the Portuguese arrived. Its pottery became an emblem of Amazonian heritage and inspired a “Marajoara” style of Brazilian art deco in the 1930s.
story.zh:
马拉若岛每年有半年被洪水淹没，岛民于是堆筑土台，有的高逾10米，占地数公顷。卡穆廷斯、帕科瓦尔等最大的土丘群上有房屋、火塘和墓地，骨灰瓮以红、黑、白三色绘有程式化的人脸和蛇纹。

20世纪80年代，美国考古学家安娜·罗斯福发掘了“动物土丘”，认为这些土丘养活了以鱼类和植物为食、由酋长统治的稠密社会。她的结论曾引起争议，但丹尼丝·沙安等人后来的研究证实了一个长期存续的区域文化。

这一传统在葡萄牙人到来之前就已衰落。其陶器成为亚马孙文化遗产的象征，并在20世纪30年代启发了巴西装饰艺术中的“马拉若拉”风格。

sources.title: Anna C. Roosevelt, Moundbuilders of the Amazon: Geophysical Archaeology on Marajó Island, Brazil (Academic Press, 1991)
Denise Pahl Schaan, Sacred Geographies of Ancient Amazonia (Left Coast Press, 2012)
Wikipedia: Marajoara culture

name.en: Tiwanaku and the Gate of the Sun

summary.en: At its height around 500–900 CE, Tiwanaku near Lake Titicaca was a city of terraced pyramids, sunken courts and precisely cut stone. The monolithic Gate of the Sun carries the Staff God flanked by winged attendants, an image that spread across the southern Andes.
summary.zh: 约公元500至900年鼎盛时期，的的喀喀湖附近的蒂瓦纳库是一座拥有阶梯金字塔、下沉式庭院和精确切割石材的城市。整石雕成的太阳门上刻有持杖神及两侧带翼的随从，这一形象传遍安第斯南部。

story.en:
Tiwanaku stood at 3,850 metres, where frost threatens crops almost every night. Its farmers built raised fields separated by water channels that stored the day’s heat and protected plants; experiments in the 1980s showed that these fields could produce far more potatoes than ordinary plots.

At the centre stood the Akapana pyramid, the Kalasasaya platform and the semi-subterranean temple with carved stone heads set in its walls. The Gate of the Sun, cut from a single block of andesite and now standing in a corner of the Kalasasaya, shows a frontal deity holding two staffs, perhaps an ancestor of the Andean creator god.

A long drought after about 1000 CE seems to have undermined the raised-field system, and the city was abandoned. When the Inca arrived they treated its ruins as a sacred place of origin.
story.zh:
蒂瓦纳库海拔3850米，几乎每夜都有霜冻威胁庄稼。农民修建以水渠相隔的台田，水渠储存白天的热量、保护作物；20世纪80年代的实验表明，这种田地的马铃薯产量远高于普通田块。

城市中心有阿卡帕纳金字塔、卡拉萨萨亚平台，以及墙上嵌有石雕人头的半地下神庙。太阳门由一整块安山岩凿成，现立于卡拉萨萨亚一角，门楣上的正面神祇手持双杖，或许是安第斯创世神的原型。

约公元1000年后的长期干旱似乎瓦解了台田体系，城市随之被遗弃。印加人到来时，将其废墟视为神圣的起源之地。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Tiwanaku: Spiritual and Political Centre of the Tiwanaku Culture
Alan L. Kolata, The Tiwanaku: Portrait of an Andean Civilization (Blackwell, 1993)
Britannica: Tiwanaku

note: The gate is usually dated to c. 500–600 CE; its original position is uncertain.

summary.en: On a ridge 3,000 m above the Utcubamba valley, the Chachapoya built a walled town whose limestone ramparts rise up to about 19 m and enclose some 400 round houses. Building began around the 6th century and the site was occupied until after the Spanish conquest.
summary.zh: 在乌特库班巴河谷上方海拔3000米的山脊上，查查波亚人修建了一座城寨，石灰岩城墙高约19米，内有约400座圆形房屋。工程约始于6世纪，直到西班牙征服之后仍有人居住。

story.en:
Kuélap is reached through three narrow gates that funnel visitors into single file, which is why it was long called a fortress. Inside, round stone houses decorated with zigzag and rhomboid friezes cluster on two levels, along with a tapering structure called the Tintero, “inkwell”.

The Chachapoya also buried their dead in cliffside tombs and in the tall clay sarcophagi of Karajía, painted with faces and topped with skulls. The Inca conquered them in the late 15th century and resettled many of them far away; when the Spanish arrived, some Chachapoya allied with the invaders.

A cable car opened in 2017 brought tourists in large numbers, but in April 2022 part of the southern wall collapsed after heavy rains, closing the site for repairs.
story.zh:
进入奎拉普要经过三道狭窄的城门，只容一人通过，因此长期被称作要塞。城内装饰着锯齿纹和菱形纹饰带的圆形石屋分布在两层台地上，还有一座上窄下宽、称为“墨水瓶”的建筑。

查查波亚人还把死者葬于悬崖墓穴和卡拉希亚高大的泥制人形石棺中，棺上绘有面孔、顶上置有头骨。15世纪末印加人征服了他们，并把许多人迁往远方；西班牙人到来时，部分查查波亚人与入侵者结盟。

2017年开通的缆车带来了大批游客，但2022年4月一场暴雨后南墙部分坍塌，遗址因修缮而关闭。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Kuélap
Warren B. Church & Adriana von Hagen, “Chachapoyas”, in Handbook of South American Archaeology (Springer, 2008)
Alfredo Narváez Vargas, Kuélap: centro del poder político religioso de los Chachapoya (2013)

note: Radiocarbon dates place the first construction around 500 CE; most building dates to c. 900–1100.

name.zh: 瓦里帝国皮基利亚克塔中心

summary.en: About 30 km south-east of Cusco, the Wari built Pikillacta, a rigidly planned compound of some 700 rooms and courts inside walls covering about 50 hectares. Its grid layout shows how the Wari state governed distant provinces centuries before the Inca.
summary.zh: 在库斯科东南约30公里处，瓦里人修建了皮基利亚克塔，这是一座规划严整的建筑群，约50公顷的围墙内有约700个房间与庭院。其网格布局显示了瓦里国家如何在印加之前数百年统治遥远的行省。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Pikillacta
Gordon F. McEwan, Pikillacta: The Wari Empire in Cuzco (University of Iowa Press, 2005)

name.en: Wari royal mausoleum of El Castillo de Huarmey
name.zh: 瓦里王室陵墓：瓦尔梅城堡

summary.en: In 2012 Polish and Peruvian archaeologists found an unlooted Wari mausoleum beneath the hill of El Castillo de Huarmey on Peru’s north-central coast. It held dozens of high-status women, including three queens, with gold ear ornaments, weaving tools and fine textiles.
summary.zh: 2012年波兰和秘鲁考古学家在秘鲁中北部海岸瓦尔梅城堡山下发现一座未被盗掘的瓦里陵墓，墓中葬有数十位高级女性，包括三位王后，随葬金耳饰、纺织工具和精美织物。

story.en:
Looters had dug at El Castillo for decades, but beneath a layer of 30 tonnes of loose gravel the team led by Miłosz Giersz and Roberto Pimentel found a chamber they had missed. Announced in 2013, it contained the remains of some 58 people, most of them women, buried seated and wrapped in textiles.

Three of the women were placed in a separate room with the richest goods: gold and silver ear spools, a ceremonial axe, bronze tools and painted ceramics from distant parts of the Wari realm. Many had been weavers, and the tools of their craft accompanied them.

The find confirmed that the Wari held the north coast directly, and that women of the elite played a central role in their empire.
story.zh:
盗墓者在瓦尔梅城堡挖掘了几十年，但由米沃什·吉尔什和罗伯托·皮门特尔领导的考古队在30吨松散砾石下发现了一个被他们遗漏的墓室。2013年公布的发现显示，墓中约有58人的遗骸，大多是女性，以坐姿下葬，身裹织物。

其中三位女性被安置在单独的墓室中，随葬品最为丰富：金银耳饰、一把礼仪斧、青铜工具以及来自瓦里疆域各地的彩陶。许多死者生前是织工，她们的工具也随之陪葬。

这一发现证实瓦里人直接统治着北部海岸，也表明精英女性在帝国中扮演着核心角色。

sources.title: Miłosz Giersz & Cecilia Pardo (eds.), Castillo de Huarmey: el mausoleo imperial wari (Museo de Arte de Lima, 2014)
National Geographic, “First Unlooted Royal Tomb of Its Kind Unearthed in Peru” (June 2013)
Wikipedia: El Castillo de Huarmey

note: The mausoleum was used over several generations, c. 750–1000 CE.

summary.en: High in the Sierra Nevada de Santa Marta, the Tairona built Teyuna on a ridge reached by some 1,200 stone steps, with about 170 circular terraces linked by paved paths and canals. Abandoned during the Spanish conquest, it was found by treasure hunters in 1972.
summary.zh: 在圣玛尔塔内华达山脉高处，泰罗纳人在山脊上修建了特尤纳，需攀登约1200级石阶方能抵达，约170座圆形台地由石铺小道和水渠相连。西班牙征服期间城市被弃，1972年被寻宝者发现。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Ciudad Perdida
ICANH, Parque Arqueológico Teyuna – Ciudad Perdida
Gerardo Reichel-Dolmatoff, Colombia (Thames & Hudson, 1965)

note: Founding is dated to around 800 CE; the Kogi, Arhuaco and Wiwa say they visited the site long before 1972.

summary.en: The Chimú capital near modern Trujillo was the largest adobe city of the Americas, covering about 20 km². Ten walled palace compounds (ciudadelas), each probably built by a successive king, held courts, storerooms, burial platforms and walk-in wells, decorated with moulded friezes of fish and seabirds.
summary.zh: 奇穆首都位于今特鲁希略附近，是美洲最大的土坯城市，面积约20平方公里。十座围墙宫殿院落（ciudadela）可能分别由历代国王修建，内有庭院、仓库、墓台和可步入的水井，墙上饰有鱼和海鸟的模印浮雕。

story.en:
A Spanish chronicle of 1604, the Historia anónima de Trujillo, preserves the Chimú tradition that a lord named Taycanamo arrived by sea on a raft of logs, founded the dynasty and ruled from the Moche valley. His successors built canals that carried water across valleys and conquered the coast from near Tumbes to the Chillón valley.

Each ciudadela of Chan Chan had towering walls up to nine metres high and a single entrance. When a king died he was buried in a platform inside his palace with his treasure and sacrificed attendants, and his successor built a new compound, as the Inca later did with royal mummies.

Topa Inca conquered Chimor around 1470, carried King Minchançaman to Cusco and deported many goldsmiths to work for the Inca. UNESCO listed Chan Chan as endangered in 1986 because heavy El Niño rains erode its unfired clay.
story.zh:
1604年的西班牙编年史《特鲁希略佚名史》保存了奇穆传说：一位名叫泰卡纳莫的领主乘木筏从海上而来，建立王朝，统治莫切河谷。其继任者修建了跨越河谷的水渠，并征服了从通贝斯附近到钦永河谷的沿海地带。

昌昌的每座宫殿院落都有高达九米的围墙和唯一的入口。国王死后，与珍宝和殉葬者一同葬于宫中的墓台，继任者则另建新的院落，这与后来印加人对待王室木乃伊的做法相似。

约1470年图帕克·印卡征服奇莫尔，将国王明昌卡曼带往库斯科，并把许多金匠迁去为印加效力。由于厄尔尼诺带来的暴雨侵蚀未经烧制的泥墙，联合国教科文组织于1986年将昌昌列为濒危遗产。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Chan Chan Archaeological Zone
Michael E. Moseley & Alana Cordy-Collins (eds.), The Northern Dynasties: Kingship and Statecraft in Chimor (Dumbarton Oaks, 1990)
Britannica: Chan Chan

note: The city’s founding is dated approximately to the 9th–10th centuries.

name.en: Garden cities of the Upper Xingu (Kuhikugu)
name.zh: 上欣古河流域的“花园城市”（库希库古）

summary.en: In the forests of the Upper Xingu, ancestors of the Kuikuro built a network of large plaza villages linked by straight roads, bridges and moats, with managed forests and fields between them. Archaeology since the 1990s shows a regional population of thousands that collapsed after European epidemics.
summary.zh: 在上欣古河的森林中，库伊库罗人的祖先修建了由笔直道路、桥梁和壕沟连接的大型广场村落网络，其间是经人工管理的林地与农田。20世纪90年代以来的考古表明，这一地区曾有数千人口，在欧洲传入的疫病后崩溃。

story.en:
Working with the Kuikuro people from 1993, the American archaeologist Michael Heckenberger mapped earthworks under the forest around their villages. He found ditches up to five metres deep, causeways oriented to the sun and the remains of settlements of up to 50 hectares, which he described in Science in 2003 and 2008.

The sites, including the one the Kuikuro call Kuhikugu, formed clusters of towns and hamlets spaced a few kilometres apart, a pattern Heckenberger compared to “garden cities”. Their soils were enriched with charcoal and refuse, the dark earth (terra preta) found across the Amazon.

The research revived the story of the British explorer Percy Fawcett, who vanished in the region in 1925 searching for a lost city he called “Z”. What he imagined as a single stone city was, it seems, a landscape of earth and wood.
story.zh:
自1993年起，美国考古学家迈克尔·赫肯伯格与库伊库罗人合作，测绘了他们村落周围森林下的土木工程遗迹。他发现了深达五米的壕沟、朝向太阳的堤道以及面积达50公顷的聚落遗址，并于2003年和2008年在《科学》杂志上发表成果。

这些遗址，包括库伊库罗人称为库希库古的地方，构成相隔数公里的城镇与村落群，赫肯伯格将其比作“花园城市”。其土壤因木炭和废弃物而肥沃，即遍布亚马孙的“黑土”。

这项研究让人重新想起英国探险家珀西·福西特：1925年他在这一地区寻找他称为“Z”的失落之城时失踪。他想象中的那座石头城，看来其实是一片由泥土和木材构成的人造景观。

sources.title: Michael J. Heckenberger et al., “Amazonia 1492: Pristine Forest or Cultural Parkland?”, Science 301 (2003)
Michael J. Heckenberger et al., “Pre-Columbian Urbanism, Anthropogenic Landscapes, and the Future of the Amazon”, Science 321 (2008)
David Grann, The Lost City of Z (Doubleday, 2009)

note: Dates are approximate; the coordinates mark the Kuikuro area of the Upper Xingu.

name.en: The El Dorado ceremony and the Muisca raft
name.zh: “黄金人”仪式与穆伊斯卡金筏

summary.en: At sacred lakes such as Guatavita, Muisca rulers made offerings of gold and emeralds. A colonial chronicle describes the new chief covered in gold dust and floated on a raft to throw treasure into the water; a small gold raft found at Pasca in 1969 shows such a scene.
summary.zh: 穆伊斯卡统治者在瓜塔维塔等圣湖投献黄金和祖母绿。殖民时期的一部编年史描述新首领全身涂满金粉、乘筏入湖抛撒珍宝；1969年在帕斯卡发现的一件小型金筏正描绘了这一场景。

story.en:
According to Juan Rodríguez Freyle, writing in Bogotá in 1636 from what he said a Muisca noble had told him, the heir to the chiefdom of Guatavita was stripped, coated with sticky earth and gold dust, and rowed to the middle of the lake with four chiefs. There he offered gold and emeralds to the waters while music sounded from the shore.

The story of el hombre dorado, “the golden man”, grew into the myth of a whole golden kingdom, and it drove Spanish, German and English expeditions deep into the Orinoco and Amazon. At Guatavita itself, the merchant Antonio de Sepúlveda cut a notch in the crater rim in the 1580s and partly drained the lake; a British company tried again in 1898–1910.

In 1969 farmers found the Muisca raft in a cave near Pasca: a cast gold figure of a chief on a raft surrounded by attendants. It is the treasure of Bogotá’s Gold Museum, and Colombia protected the lake from treasure-hunting in 1965.
story.zh:
据胡安·罗德里格斯·弗雷伊莱1636年在波哥大的记载（他称来自一位穆伊斯卡贵族的讲述），瓜塔维塔酋邦的继承人被脱去衣物，全身涂上黏土和金粉，与四位首领一同被划到湖心，在岸边的乐声中向湖水献上黄金和祖母绿。

“镀金之人”（el hombre dorado）的故事演变为整个黄金王国的神话，驱使西班牙、德意志和英格兰的远征队深入奥里诺科河与亚马孙河流域。在瓜塔维塔湖本身，商人安东尼奥·德·塞普尔韦达于16世纪80年代在火山口边缘开凿缺口，部分排干湖水；1898至1910年一家英国公司再度尝试。

1969年农民在帕斯卡附近的一个洞穴中发现了穆伊斯卡金筏：一件铸金作品，表现首领立于筏上、侍从环绕。它是波哥大黄金博物馆的镇馆之宝。哥伦比亚于1965年立法禁止在湖中寻宝。

sources.title: Juan Rodríguez Freyle, El Carnero (1636), ch. 2
Banco de la República, Museo del Oro: Balsa muisca
Wikipedia: El Dorado

note: The ceremony is known from one colonial account written a century after the conquest; the raft is dated roughly to 1200–1500.

name.zh: 亚瓦尔潘帕战役（昌卡战争）

summary.en: According to Inca tradition, the Chanka confederation attacked Cusco and the prince Cusi Yupanqui, abandoned by his father, defended the city and then routed the Chanka on the “plain of blood”. The victory made him Sapa Inca as Pachacuti and began the Inca expansion.
summary.zh: 据印加传说，昌卡联盟进攻库斯科，被父亲抛弃的王子库西·尤潘基坚守城池，随后在“血之平原”击溃昌卡人。这场胜利使他以帕查库蒂之名成为萨帕印卡，开启了印加的扩张。

sources.title: Juan de Betanzos, Suma y narración de los Incas (1551)
Brian S. Bauer, The Development of the Inca State (University of Texas Press, 1992)
Wikipedia: Chanka–Inca War

note: Known only from Inca oral tradition recorded after 1532; some scholars doubt the war happened as told. 1438 is a conventional date.

name.en: Pachacuti rebuilds Cusco and the Coricancha
name.zh: 帕查库蒂重建库斯科与科里坎查

summary.en: After defeating the Chanka, Pachacuti rebuilt Cusco as an imperial capital of fitted stone, draining marshes and canalising its rivers. Its centre was the Coricancha, the “golden enclosure” of the Sun, from which 41 lines of shrines (ceques) radiated across the valley.
summary.zh: 击败昌卡人后，帕查库蒂用精密砌石把库斯科重建为帝国首都，排干沼泽、疏导河流。城市中心是科里坎查——太阳神的“黄金围场”，41条神龛线（ceque）由此向整个河谷辐射。

sources.title: Brian S. Bauer, Ancient Cuzco: Heartland of the Inca (University of Texas Press, 2004)
Bernabé Cobo, Historia del Nuevo Mundo (1653), book XIII
Wikipedia: Coricancha

note: The rebuilding is attributed by the chroniclers to Pachacuti; exact dates are unknown.

summary.en: On a saddle between two peaks above the Urubamba gorge, Inca masons built a royal estate of temples, palaces, terraces and fountains for Pachacuti. Occupied by a few hundred people, it was abandoned around the Spanish conquest and never found by the conquerors.
summary.zh: 在乌鲁班巴峡谷上方两座山峰之间的鞍部，印加石匠为帕查库蒂修建了一座王室庄园，有神庙、宫殿、梯田和泉池。这里常住数百人，西班牙征服前后被弃，征服者从未发现它。

story.en:
Machu Picchu was not a city but a country retreat, where the Inca emperor and his household came to rest, hunt and worship. Its builders cut granite from the mountain itself and laid foundations and drains so well that more than half the construction is below ground; the site survives earthquakes and heavy rain to this day.

Its finest buildings, the Temple of the Sun with its curved wall, the Intihuatana stone and the Temple of the Three Windows, show the most refined Inca masonry. Colonial land records of 1568, published by the archaeologist John Rowe, place the Picchu lands in Pachacuti’s estate, which is why most scholars attribute the site to his lineage.

Radiocarbon dating published in 2021 by Richard Burger and colleagues showed the site was occupied from around 1420, two decades earlier than the date drawn from Spanish chronicles. It became a UNESCO World Heritage site in 1983.
story.zh:
马丘比丘并非城市，而是一处乡间行宫，印加皇帝和王室成员来此休憩、狩猎和祭祀。建造者直接从山体开采花岗岩，地基和排水系统极为考究，一半以上的工程位于地下，因此至今仍能抵御地震和暴雨。

最精美的建筑——带弧形墙的太阳神庙、拴日石和三窗神庙——代表了印加砌石技艺的最高水平。考古学家约翰·罗发表的1568年殖民地土地文书将皮丘一带的土地归于帕查库蒂的庄园，因此多数学者认为此地属于他的家族。

2021年理查德·伯格等人发表的放射性碳测年显示，此地约从1420年起就有人居住，比根据西班牙编年史推算的时间早二十年。1983年它被列入联合国教科文组织世界遗产名录。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Historic Sanctuary of Machu Picchu
Britannica: Machu Picchu
Richard L. Burger et al., “New AMS dates for Machu Picchu”, Antiquity 95 (2021)

note: Chronicle-based chronology puts construction after c. 1450; AMS dates suggest occupation from c. 1420.

name.en: Qhapaq Ñan, the Inca road system

summary.en: The Inca linked their empire with some 30,000–40,000 km of roads running along the coast and the Andes from southern Colombia to central Chile. Relay runners (chaskis), way stations (tambos) and suspension bridges of woven grass let orders and goods travel quickly without wheels or horses.
summary.zh: 印加人以约3万至4万公里的道路连通帝国，沿海岸和安第斯山脉从哥伦比亚南部延伸至智利中部。驿跑者（chaski）、驿站（tambo）和草编吊桥使命令与物资在没有车轮和马匹的情况下迅速传递。

label.en: Northern frontier near Pasto and Caranqui
label.zh: 北部边界（帕斯托与卡兰基附近）
基多
图米班巴
卡哈马卡
瓦努科潘帕
哈通豪哈

label.zh: 库斯科，四方的中枢
的的喀喀湖畔哈通科利亚

label.en: Altiplano road to Paria and Chicha country
label.zh: 经帕里亚前往奇查地区的高原道路
马波乔河谷（圣地亚哥）

story.en:
The two main trunk routes ran north–south, one along the coastal desert and one through the highlands, joined by dozens of cross-roads. Roads were paved, stepped or cut into rock where needed, and every 20 km or so stood a tambo with lodging and storehouses for armies and officials.

Teams of chaskis waiting in small huts passed messages and knotted khipu records from runner to runner; the Spanish reported that news could cross 240 km a day and that fresh fish reached the emperor in Cusco from the coast. Rope bridges spanned the gorges; one, the Q’eswachaka, is still rewoven every year by four Quechua communities.

The roads served the Spanish conquerors as well, carrying Pizarro to Cajamarca and Cusco. In 2014 UNESCO listed 616 km of the network across six countries as a single World Heritage site.
story.zh:
两条主干道南北纵贯，一条沿海岸荒漠，一条穿越高原，数十条横向道路将其连接。需要时道路铺石、修筑台阶或在岩壁上开凿，每隔约20公里设一座驿站，为军队和官员提供住宿与仓储。

在小屋中守候的驿跑者接力传递口信和结绳记录；据西班牙人记载，消息一天可传240公里，海边的鲜鱼也能送到库斯科皇帝的餐桌上。绳索吊桥横跨峡谷，其中的克斯瓦查卡桥至今仍由四个克丘亚社区每年重新编织。

这些道路同样为西班牙征服者所用，把皮萨罗带到卡哈马卡和库斯科。2014年联合国教科文组织将横跨六国的616公里路段列为一处世界遗产。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Qhapaq Ñan, Andean Road System
John Hyslop, The Inka Road System (Academic Press, 1984)
Pedro Cieza de León, Crónica del Perú, part I (1553)

note: Many segments are older (Wari and earlier); the Inca integrated them into one system from the mid-15th century.

name.zh: 尤耶亚科火山上的“卡帕科查”献祭

summary.en: Around 1500, three Inca children were taken in a state ceremony from Cusco to the summit of the 6,739 m volcano Llullaillaco and buried as offerings. Found frozen in 1999 by Johan Reinhard and Constanza Ceruti, they are among the best-preserved mummies in the world.
summary.zh: 约1500年，三名印加儿童在一场国家仪式中从库斯科被带到海拔6739米的尤耶亚科火山顶，作为祭品被埋葬。1999年约翰·莱因哈德和康斯坦萨·塞鲁蒂发现了冻结的遗体，它们是世界上保存最好的木乃伊之一。

story.en:
The capacocha was among the most solemn Inca rites. Children chosen for their beauty and status were feasted in Cusco, then led along the roads to the provinces and up the highest mountains, binding the empire and its sacred peaks together.

On Llullaillaco, on today’s Argentine–Chilean border, the Inca built stone platforms near the summit. The expedition of 1999 found a girl of about 13, known as the Maiden, and a younger boy and girl, seated with textiles, figurines and food. Chemical analysis of the Maiden’s hair showed that her diet improved and her use of coca and alcohol rose sharply in her final year.

The children now rest in a museum in Salta, displayed one at a time in freezing cases, which some Indigenous groups regard as disrespectful.
story.zh:
“卡帕科查”是印加最庄严的仪式之一。因容貌和身份而被选中的孩子在库斯科接受宴请，随后沿驿道被送往各省，登上最高的山峰，以此把帝国与神圣的山峰联结在一起。

印加人在今阿根廷与智利边境的尤耶亚科峰顶附近修建了石台。1999年的考察队发现一位约13岁的少女（称为“少女”）以及一对年幼的男孩和女孩，他们呈坐姿，身边有织物、小雕像和食物。对“少女”头发的化学分析显示，她在生命最后一年饮食改善，古柯和酒的摄入急剧增加。

这些孩子如今安放在萨尔塔的一座博物馆中，每次只在冷冻展柜中展出一具，一些原住民团体认为这有失尊重。

sources.title: Johan Reinhard & Constanza Ceruti, Inca Rituals and Sacred Mountains (Cotsen Institute, 2010)
Andrew S. Wilson et al., “Stable isotope and DNA evidence for ritual sequences in Inca child sacrifice”, PNAS 104 (2007)
Wikipedia: Mummies of Llullaillaco

name.en: Columbus reaches the South American mainland

summary.en: On his third voyage Columbus sailed south of Trinidad and landed on the Paria peninsula of Venezuela in August 1498, the first recorded European landing on the South American mainland. The volume of fresh water from the Orinoco convinced him he had found “another world”.
summary.zh: 第三次航行中，哥伦布驶过特立尼达以南，于1498年8月在委内瑞拉帕里亚半岛登陆，这是有记载的欧洲人首次踏上南美大陆。奥里诺科河涌出的大量淡水使他相信自己发现了“另一个世界”。

佛得角群岛

帕里亚半岛（8月5日）

Samuel Eliot Morison, Admiral of the Ocean Sea (Little, Brown, 1942)

name.zh: 卡布拉尔船队抵达巴西

summary.en: Sailing for India, Pedro Álvares Cabral’s 13 ships swung far west and on 22 April 1500 sighted Monte Pascoal on the coast of Bahia. The Portuguese stayed ten days, held the first Mass and claimed the “Land of the True Cross” for King Manuel I before continuing to Calicut.
summary.zh: 佩德罗·阿尔瓦雷斯·卡布拉尔率13艘船前往印度，向西远航，于1500年4月22日望见巴伊亚海岸的帕斯科亚尔山。葡萄牙人停留十天，举行了第一次弥撒，为曼努埃尔一世宣称“真十字架之地”，随后继续驶往卡利卡特。

label.zh: 自里斯本启航（3月9日）
经过佛得角群岛

label.en: Anchors at Porto Seguro, Brazil (22 April)
label.zh: 在巴西塞古罗港停泊（4月22日）

label.en: Loses four ships off the Cape of Good Hope
label.zh: 在好望角外海损失四艘船
抵达卡利卡特（9月13日）
返回里斯本

story.en:
The fleet that left Lisbon on 9 March 1500 was the largest Portugal had yet sent to India. Following Vasco da Gama’s advice to swing wide into the Atlantic to catch the winds, it drifted, by accident or design, far enough west to sight land on 22 April, Easter week.

The scribe Pero Vaz de Caminha wrote a long letter to the king describing the Tupiniquim people who met them on the beach, painted and unashamed of their nakedness, trading feathered headdresses for caps and bells. On 26 April the friar Henrique de Coimbra said Mass under a great wooden cross while the local people watched and imitated the kneeling sailors.

Cabral sent a supply ship back to Lisbon with the news, left two convicts ashore to learn the language and sailed on. Caminha’s letter lay forgotten in the archives until 1773, but the brazilwood trade soon gave the new land its name.
story.zh:
1500年3月9日离开里斯本的船队，是葡萄牙迄今派往印度规模最大的一支。船队听从瓦斯科·达伽马的建议，深入大西洋借风航行，无论出于偶然还是有意，向西漂得足够远，于4月22日复活节周望见陆地。

书记官佩罗·瓦斯·德·卡米尼亚给国王写了一封长信，描述在海滩上迎接他们的图皮尼金人：他们身涂彩绘，对裸体毫不羞涩，用羽毛头饰交换帽子和铃铛。4月26日，恩里克·德·科英布拉修士在一座高大的木十字架下主持弥撒，当地人在旁观看，并模仿水手们跪拜。

卡布拉尔派一艘补给船回里斯本报信，留下两名罪犯在岸上学习语言，随后继续航行。卡米尼亚的信在档案馆中被遗忘，直到1773年才重见天日，而巴西木贸易很快赋予了这片新土地名字。

sources.title: Pero Vaz de Caminha, Carta a el-Rei D. Manuel (1 May 1500), Torre do Tombo
Britannica: Pedro Álvares Cabral
Boris Fausto, A Concise History of Brazil (Cambridge UP, 1999)

summary.en: After Huayna Capac and his chosen heir died in an epidemic, his sons Huáscar in Cusco and Atahualpa with the veteran northern armies in Quito fought for the throne. Atahualpa’s generals Quisquis and Chalcuchimac captured Huáscar near Cusco in 1532, just as the Spanish arrived.
summary.zh: 瓦伊纳·卡帕克及其指定继承人死于瘟疫后，他的儿子——坐镇库斯科的瓦斯卡尔与统率北方老兵、驻守基多的阿塔瓦尔帕——争夺王位。1532年阿塔瓦尔帕的将领基斯基斯和查尔库奇马克在库斯科附近俘获瓦斯卡尔，恰在此时西班牙人到来。

label.zh: 阿塔瓦尔帕的根据地基多
图米班巴一带的战斗
瓦斯卡尔军在钦博拉索附近战败
北方军经豪哈推进

label.en: Huáscar captured at Quipaipan near Cusco
label.zh: 瓦斯卡尔在库斯科附近基派潘被俘

story.en:
Huayna Capac spent his last years in the north and died around 1527, probably of smallpox that had spread ahead of the Europeans; his designated heir Ninan Cuyochi died at about the same time. Huáscar was recognised in Cusco, while Atahualpa remained in Quito with the army that had campaigned there for years.

The rivalry turned into open war. According to the chroniclers, Atahualpa’s forces won a series of battles southward, and in 1532 Quisquis and Chalcuchimac routed Huáscar at Quipaipan and captured him. They then massacred members of his family and of Topa Inca’s lineage in Cusco.

Atahualpa was travelling south to take the capital when he learned of strange bearded men on the coast. The war had divided the Inca nobility, and many of Huáscar’s supporters at first welcomed the Spanish as allies.
story.zh:
瓦伊纳·卡帕克晚年驻于北方，约1527年去世，很可能死于先于欧洲人传入的天花；他指定的继承人尼南·库约奇几乎同时死去。库斯科拥立了瓦斯卡尔，而阿塔瓦尔帕则与在北方征战多年的军队留在基多。

对立演变为公开的战争。据编年史记载，阿塔瓦尔帕的军队一路南下连战连胜，1532年基斯基斯和查尔库奇马克在基派潘击溃瓦斯卡尔并将其俘获，随后在库斯科屠杀了他的家族以及图帕克·印卡一系的成员。

阿塔瓦尔帕正南下接管首都时，得知海岸出现了奇怪的长须人。内战分裂了印加贵族，瓦斯卡尔的许多支持者起初把西班牙人当作盟友来欢迎。

sources.title: Britannica: Atahuallpa
Juan de Betanzos, Suma y narración de los Incas (1551), part II
John Hemming, The Conquest of the Incas (1970)

note: Dates and the sequence of battles differ between chroniclers.

name.zh: 卡哈马卡擒获阿塔瓦尔帕

summary.en: On 16 November 1532 Francisco Pizarro’s 168 men ambushed Atahualpa’s unarmed retinue in the main square of Cajamarca, killing thousands and taking the Inca prisoner. The capture paralysed the empire; Atahualpa paid a vast ransom in gold and silver but was executed in July 1533.
summary.zh: 1532年11月16日，弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗的168人在卡哈马卡中央广场伏击阿塔瓦尔帕未带武器的随从，杀死数千人并俘获印加君主。此举使帝国陷入瘫痪；阿塔瓦尔帕交付了巨额金银赎金，仍于1533年7月被处决。

label.zh: 皮萨罗自巴拿马启航

label.en: Puná island in the Gulf of Guayaquil
label.zh: 瓜亚基尔湾普纳岛

label.en: Tumbes, found ruined by the civil war
label.zh: 通贝斯，已毁于内战
建立圣米格尔-德皮乌拉
登上安第斯山
卡哈马卡（11月15–16日）

story.en:
Pizarro’s men reached Cajamarca on 15 November 1532 and found the town empty, with Atahualpa’s army camped on the hillsides around the baths. That night, according to their own accounts, many Spaniards were too frightened to sleep. Pizarro hid his cavalry and a few small cannon in the long halls around the square.

Atahualpa arrived late the next afternoon on a litter, surrounded by thousands of attendants who carried no weapons. The Dominican friar Vicente de Valverde came forward with a breviary and the requirement that the Inca submit; when the book fell to the ground, Pizarro gave the signal. Guns, trumpets and charging horses caused panic, and the Spaniards killed for hours while Pizarro himself pulled Atahualpa from his litter.

No Spaniard was killed. The ransom gathered from across the empire filled a room about 6.2 by 4.8 metres to the height of a raised arm with gold; the “Ransom Room” still stands in Cajamarca.
story.zh:
1532年11月15日，皮萨罗一行抵达卡哈马卡，发现城中空无一人，阿塔瓦尔帕的军队驻扎在温泉周围的山坡上。据他们自己的记述，当夜许多西班牙人吓得无法入睡。皮萨罗把骑兵和几门小炮藏在广场周围的长厅里。

次日傍晚，阿塔瓦尔帕乘轿而来，数千名未带武器的侍从簇拥左右。多明我会修士比森特·德·巴尔韦德手持祈祷书上前，宣读要求印加臣服的“劝降书”；书掉落在地时，皮萨罗发出信号。枪声、号角和冲锋的战马引发恐慌，西班牙人屠杀了数小时，皮萨罗亲手把阿塔瓦尔帕从轿上拽下。

西班牙人无一阵亡。从帝国各地搜集来的赎金把一间约6.2米长、4.8米宽的房间填满黄金，高度达举起手臂所及之处；这间“赎金屋”至今仍矗立在卡哈马卡。

sources.title: Francisco de Xerez, Verdadera relación de la conquista del Perú (1534)
James Lockhart, The Men of Cajamarca (University of Texas Press, 1972)
Britannica: Francisco Pizarro

name.en: Spanish conquest of the Inca Empire

summary.en: From the capture of Atahualpa to the fall of Vilcabamba, a few thousand Spaniards with tens of thousands of Andean allies took over Tawantinsuyu, helped by epidemics, the civil war and the Inca nobility’s divisions. The conquest also unleashed civil wars among the conquistadors themselves.
summary.zh: 从擒获阿塔瓦尔帕到比尔卡班巴陷落，数千西班牙人与数万安第斯盟军夺取了塔万廷苏尤，疫病、内战和印加贵族的分裂都助了他们一臂之力。征服还引发了征服者之间的内战。

攻占豪哈，俘获查尔库奇马克

label.en: Battle of Jaquijahuana ends the conquistador civil wars
label.zh: 哈基哈瓦纳战役结束征服者内战
比尔卡班巴陷落

story.en:
Pizarro’s capture of Atahualpa gave the Spanish a hostage and a fortune. After executing him, they marched south with Inca allies who hated Atahualpa’s generals, and installed Manco Inca as a puppet in Cusco. Smallpox and other diseases had already killed many people and kept on killing.

In 1536 Manco rebelled and nearly destroyed the Spanish, who held out in Cusco for ten months. Meanwhile the conquerors turned on each other: Diego de Almagro was defeated at Las Salinas and executed in 1538, his followers murdered Pizarro in 1541, and Gonzalo Pizarro’s rebellion against the New Laws ended only at Jaquijahuana in 1548.

Manco’s heirs held out in Vilcabamba for 35 years. Viceroy Francisco de Toledo, determined to end Inca sovereignty, took the refuge in 1572 and executed Túpac Amaru, then reorganised Andean society into reducciones and the Potosí mita.
story.zh:
皮萨罗擒获阿塔瓦尔帕，使西班牙人手握人质和巨额财富。处决阿塔瓦尔帕后，他们与痛恨其将领的印加盟军一同南下，在库斯科扶植曼科·印卡为傀儡。天花等疫病此前已夺去大量生命，并继续蔓延。

1536年曼科起兵，几乎消灭了西班牙人，后者在库斯科坚守了十个月。与此同时，征服者内部反目：迭戈·德·阿尔马格罗在拉斯萨利纳斯战败，1538年被处决；其追随者于1541年刺杀皮萨罗；贡萨洛·皮萨罗反对《新法》的叛乱直到1548年哈基哈瓦纳战役才告平息。

曼科的继承者在比尔卡班巴坚持了35年。决心终结印加主权的总督弗朗西斯科·德·托莱多于1572年攻占这一避难所，处决图帕克·阿马鲁，随后把安第斯社会重组为集中村镇（reducción）和波托西矿役制度。

sources.title: John Hemming, The Conquest of the Incas (Macmillan, 1970)
Britannica: Inca: The Spanish conquest
Kim MacQuarrie, The Last Days of the Incas (Simon & Schuster, 2007)

summary.en: Francisco Pizarro founded the City of the Kings on the Rímac river on 18 January 1535, choosing a coastal site that could be supplied by sea from Panama. It became the capital of the Viceroyalty of Peru and the centre of Spanish power in South America.
summary.zh: 1535年1月18日，弗朗西斯科·皮萨罗在里马克河畔建立“诸王之城”，选址于可经海路从巴拿马获得补给的海岸。它后来成为秘鲁总督区首府和西班牙在南美的权力中心。

sources.title: Britannica: Lima
Bernabé Cobo, Historia de la fundación de Lima (1639)
UNESCO World Heritage: Historic Centre of Lima

summary.en: Manco Inca escaped Spanish custody and in May 1536 surrounded Cusco with a vast army, setting the thatched roofs ablaze. The 190 Spaniards and their Indigenous allies held out, stormed the fortress of Saqsaywaman, where Juan Pizarro was killed, and survived until relief arrived in 1537.
summary.zh: 曼科·印卡逃脱西班牙人的看管，1536年5月率大军包围库斯科，点燃城中茅草屋顶。190名西班牙人及其原住民盟军坚守不退，强攻萨克塞华曼要塞（胡安·皮萨罗在此战死），一直撑到1537年援军抵达。

story.en:
Manco had been humiliated by Pizarro’s brothers, who imprisoned him and seized his wives. He slipped out of Cusco in April 1536 on the pretext of bringing back a golden statue, and gathered an army reported at 100,000 or more.

In May the besiegers hurled red-hot stones wrapped in cotton onto the roofs, and most of the city burned. The Spaniards, with Cañari and Chachapoya allies, broke out and took the fortress of Saqsaywaman in a night assault, during which Juan Pizarro died from a sling-stone to the head. An Inca noble, according to the chroniclers, fought on its towers until he threw himself from the walls.

The siege faded as farmers had to return to plant. In 1537 Manco beat back Hernando Pizarro at Ollantaytambo by flooding the plain, then withdrew to Vilcabamba.
story.zh:
曼科曾遭皮萨罗兄弟羞辱，被他们囚禁，妻妾被夺。1536年4月，他借口取回一尊金像溜出库斯科，聚集起据说多达十万甚至更多的军队。

5月，围城者把裹着棉花的烧红石块抛上屋顶，城市大部分被焚毁。西班牙人与卡尼亚里和查查波亚盟军突围，在夜袭中攻占萨克塞华曼要塞，胡安·皮萨罗被投石击中头部身亡。据编年史记载，一名印加贵族在塔楼上奋战到底，最后从城墙上纵身跃下。

由于农民需要回乡播种，围城逐渐松懈。1537年曼科在奥扬泰坦博引水淹没平原，击退埃尔南多·皮萨罗，随后撤往比尔卡班巴。

sources.title: Titu Cusi Yupanqui, Instrucción (1570)
Pedro Pizarro, Relación del descubrimiento y conquista de los reinos del Perú (1571)
John Hemming, The Conquest of the Incas (1970)

name.en: Spanish conquest of the Muisca and founding of Bogotá
name.zh: 西班牙征服穆伊斯卡与波哥大建城

summary.en: Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada led an expedition from Santa Marta up the Magdalena river to the Muisca highlands, seized the treasure of the zaque of Hunza and founded Santa Fe de Bogotá in August 1538. The rival expeditions of Federmann and Belalcázar arrived in 1539.
summary.zh: 贡萨洛·希门尼斯·德·克萨达率远征队从圣玛尔塔沿马格达莱纳河而上抵达穆伊斯卡高原，夺取洪萨萨克的财宝，于1538年8月建立圣菲波哥大。1539年费德曼和贝拉尔卡萨尔的远征队相继到达。

label.zh: 离开圣玛尔塔（4月）

label.en: Struggles up the Magdalena to La Tora
label.zh: 沿马格达莱纳河艰难上溯至拉托拉

label.zh: 在贝莱斯附近登上高原
洗劫洪萨（通哈）
建立圣菲波哥大

sources.title: Juan Friede, Gonzalo Jiménez de Quesada a través de documentos históricos (1960)
Juan de Castellanos, Elegías de varones ilustres de Indias (1589)
Wikipedia: Spanish conquest of the Muisca

name.zh: 奥雷亚纳的亚马孙河之旅

summary.en: Separated from Gonzalo Pizarro’s starving expedition, Francisco de Orellana and some 50 men built a brigantine and drifted down the Napo and the Amazon for eight months, reaching the Atlantic in August 1542. Friar Gaspar de Carvajal’s account of dense riverbank societies and warrior women gave the river its name.
summary.zh: 弗朗西斯科·德·奥雷亚纳与约50人脱离贡萨洛·皮萨罗饥饿的远征队，造了一艘双桅船，沿纳波河和亚马孙河漂流八个月，于1542年8月抵达大西洋。加斯帕尔·德·卡瓦哈尔修士对河岸稠密社会和女战士的记述使这条河得名“亚马孙”。

label.zh: 随贡萨洛·皮萨罗离开基多（2月）
在纳波河上分道（12月）
进入亚马孙河（2月）

label.en: Fights the people of Machiparo and the Omagua
label.zh: 与马奇帕罗人和奥马瓜人交战

label.en: Passes the mouth of the Rio Negro (June)
label.zh: 经过内格罗河口（6月）

label.en: Battle with the “Amazons” near the Nhamundá
label.zh: 在尼亚蒙达河附近与“亚马孙女战士”交战
抵达大西洋（8月）
抵达库巴瓜岛（9月）

story.en:
Gonzalo Pizarro set out from Quito in 1541 to find the “Land of Cinnamon” with more than 200 Spaniards and thousands of Indigenous porters, most of whom died. On the Napo, starving, he sent his lieutenant Orellana ahead in a newly built boat to look for food. The current was too strong to return, and Orellana chose, or was forced, to go on.

For eight months the party drifted down the greatest river on Earth. The Dominican friar Gaspar de Carvajal, who lost an eye to an arrow, described villages stretching for leagues along the banks, roads leading inland and fine painted pottery. In June 1542 they fought warriors led, he wrote, by tall fair women like the Amazons of Greek legend.

Later travellers found the banks almost empty and dismissed Carvajal as a fabulist. Archaeology has since shown that large populations did live along the river and collapsed after European diseases arrived, making his chronicle a rare glimpse of the Amazon before the collapse.
story.zh:
1541年，贡萨洛·皮萨罗率200多名西班牙人和数千名原住民挑夫从基多出发寻找“肉桂之乡”，挑夫大多死于途中。在纳波河上饥饿难耐时，他派副手奥雷亚纳乘新造的船先行寻找食物。水流太急无法返回，奥雷亚纳选择（或被迫）继续前行。

一行人在地球上最大的河流上漂流了八个月。被箭射瞎一只眼的多明我会修士加斯帕尔·德·卡瓦哈尔记载，河岸上的村落绵延数里格，道路通向内陆，彩陶精美。1542年6月他们与一群战士交战，他写道，率领这些战士的是身材高大、肤色白皙的女子，宛如希腊传说中的亚马孙人。

后来的旅行者发现河岸几乎荒无人烟，便斥卡瓦哈尔为杜撰者。考古学后来证明，沿河确实曾有大量人口，在欧洲疫病传入后崩溃，他的编年史因而成为窥见崩溃前亚马孙的罕见史料。

sources.title: Gaspar de Carvajal, Relación del nuevo descubrimiento del famoso río Grande (1542)
Britannica: Francisco de Orellana
Charles C. Mann, 1491: New Revelations of the Americas Before Columbus (Knopf, 2005)

summary.en: In 1545 an Andean herder, by tradition named Diego Huallpa, found silver ore on the Cerro Rico, a mountain at over 4,700 m in today’s Bolivia. Potosí became the largest silver source in the world; worked by mita conscripts, it fed the Spanish treasury and the trade of Ming China.
summary.zh: 1545年，一位安第斯牧人（相传名叫迭戈·瓦利帕）在今玻利维亚海拔4700余米的里科山上发现银矿。波托西成为世界最大的白银来源；在矿役劳工的劳作下，它充实了西班牙国库，也推动了明代中国的贸易。

story.en:
Legend says Diego Huallpa lit a fire on the mountainside to keep warm and saw molten silver run from the rocks. Within a year thousands of prospectors had arrived, and by around 1600 Potosí, at 4,000 metres in a barren puna, may have held 100,000 people or more, among the largest cities in the Western world.

When the rich surface ores ran out, Viceroy Francisco de Toledo introduced mercury amalgamation, using mercury from Huancavelica, and in 1573 organised the mita, which forced about one in seven adult men of 16 highland provinces to work in the mines in rotation. Thousands died from accidents, mercury poisoning and cold, and the mountain earned the name “the mountain that eats men”.

Coins struck at the Potosí mint crossed the Atlantic to Seville and the Pacific on the Manila galleons, where Chinese merchants exchanged silk and porcelain for silver. The phrase “vale un Potosí”, “worth a Potosí”, entered Spanish as a byword for riches.
story.zh:
相传迭戈·瓦利帕在山坡上生火取暖，看见熔化的白银从岩石中流出。不到一年便有数千名探矿者蜂拥而至；约1600年时，位于海拔4000米荒凉高原上的波托西人口或达十万以上，是西方世界最大的城市之一。

地表富矿采尽后，总督弗朗西斯科·德·托莱多引入使用万卡韦利卡水银的汞齐法，并于1573年建立矿役制度，强制高原16个省约七分之一的成年男子轮流下矿。成千上万人死于事故、汞中毒和严寒，这座山因此被称为“吃人的山”。

波托西造币厂铸造的银币横渡大西洋运往塞维利亚，又随马尼拉大帆船越过太平洋，中国商人在那里以丝绸和瓷器换取白银。“价值一个波托西”（vale un Potosí）从此成为西班牙语中形容巨富的俗语。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: City of Potosí
Kris Lane, Potosí: The Silver City That Changed the World (University of California Press, 2019)
Peter Bakewell, Miners of the Red Mountain: Indian Labor in Potosí, 1545–1650 (University of New Mexico Press, 1984)

note: Population estimates for c. 1600–1611 range from about 100,000 to 160,000.

name.en: University of San Marcos founded in Lima
name.zh: 利马圣马科斯大学创立

summary.en: A royal decree of Charles V on 12 May 1551 created the Royal University of Lima, later named San Marcos. It is the oldest officially chartered university in the Americas and trained clergy, lawyers and, from the 18th century, physicians for the viceroyalty.
summary.zh: 1551年5月12日，查理五世颁布敕令设立利马王家大学，后称圣马科斯大学。它是美洲最早获官方特许的大学，为总督区培养教士、律师，18世纪起也培养医生。

sources.title: Wikipedia: National University of San Marcos
Luis Antonio Eguiguren, Historia de la Universidad de San Marcos (1951)

summary.en: On Christmas Day 1553 Mapuche warriors led by Lautaro, Valdivia’s former groom, attacked in successive waves to exhaust the Spanish cavalry outside the fort of Tucapel. The governor Pedro de Valdivia was captured and killed, a defeat that opened three centuries of Mapuche independence.
summary.zh: 1553年圣诞节，瓦尔迪维亚昔日的马夫劳塔罗率马普切战士在图卡佩尔要塞外分波次轮番进攻，拖垮西班牙骑兵。总督佩德罗·德·瓦尔迪维亚被俘遇害，这场失败开启了马普切人三个世纪的独立。

sources.title: Britannica: Pedro de Valdivia
Jerónimo de Vivar, Crónica y relación copiosa y verdadera de los reinos de Chile (1558)
Alonso de Ercilla, La Araucana (1569)

note: Usually dated 25 December 1553; some sources place Valdivia’s death on 1 January 1554.

summary.en: A century of warfare between Spanish Chile and the Mapuche, who adopted horses and pikes and destroyed every Spanish town south of the Biobío in 1598–1604. The Parliament of Quilín in 1641 recognised the river as a frontier; fighting flared repeatedly until the 1650s.
summary.zh: 西属智利与马普切人之间长达一个世纪的战争。马普切人学会使用马匹和长矛，1598至1604年间摧毁了比奥比奥河以南所有西班牙城镇。1641年基林议会承认该河为边界，战事直到17世纪50年代仍屡次爆发。

图卡佩尔：瓦尔迪维亚被杀
劳塔罗在马塔基托阵亡

story.en:
Valdivia expected the southern valleys to yield gold and Indigenous labour as Peru had. Instead the Mapuche, who had already stopped the Inca, organised under elected war leaders (toquis), learned to fight Spanish cavalry with long pikes and ambushes, and from the 1560s rode horses themselves.

The Spanish poet-soldier Alonso de Ercilla fought in these campaigns and wrote La Araucana, an epic that turned the Mapuche chiefs Caupolicán and Lautaro into heroic figures for European readers. In 1598 the toqui Pelantaro killed the governor at Curalaba, and within six years the Mapuche had destroyed the seven Spanish towns of the south.

Spain eventually settled for a fortified frontier along the Biobío with a professional army paid from Peru, and for treaty councils (parlamentos) with Mapuche leaders. Mapuche independence lasted until Chile and Argentina conquered their lands in the 1880s.
story.zh:
瓦尔迪维亚指望南方河谷能像秘鲁一样提供黄金和原住民劳力。然而曾经挡住印加人的马普切人在推选出的战争首领（托基）领导下组织起来，学会用长矛和伏击对付西班牙骑兵，并从16世纪60年代起自己也骑上了马。

西班牙诗人兼军人阿隆索·德·埃尔西利亚参加过这些战役，写下史诗《阿劳加纳》，把马普切首领考波利坎和劳塔罗塑造成欧洲读者心目中的英雄。1598年托基佩兰塔罗在库拉拉瓦杀死总督，此后六年间马普切人摧毁了南方七座西班牙城镇。

西班牙最终接受了沿比奥比奥河设防的边界，由秘鲁出资供养职业军队，并与马普切首领举行议会（parlamento）缔约。马普切人的独立一直持续到19世纪80年代智利和阿根廷征服其土地为止。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Arauco War
Alonso de Ercilla, La Araucana (1569–1589)
José Bengoa, Historia del pueblo mapuche (Ediciones Sur, 1985)

note: Start and end dates vary: some historians date the war from 1536 or 1550 and extend it to the 1820s.

name.en: France Antarctique and the founding of Rio de Janeiro
name.zh: 南极法兰西与里约热内卢建城

summary.en: In 1555 Admiral Villegaignon founded a French colony on an island in Guanabara Bay, allied with the Tupinambá. To expel it, the Portuguese under Estácio de Sá founded São Sebastião do Rio de Janeiro in 1565 and destroyed the last French positions in 1567.
summary.zh: 1555年海军将领维尔加尼翁在瓜纳巴拉湾的一座岛上建立法国殖民地，并与图皮南巴人结盟。为驱逐法国人，葡萄牙人在埃斯塔西奥·德·萨率领下于1565年建立圣塞巴斯蒂昂-杜里约热内卢，1567年摧毁法国人的最后据点。

story.en:
Nicolas Durand de Villegaignon, a Knight of Malta, persuaded Admiral Coligny and King Henry II to back a colony in Brazil, and in 1555 built Fort Coligny on a small island in Guanabara Bay. Calvin sent Protestant ministers from Geneva, but quarrels over the Eucharist split the colony and Villegaignon had several Huguenots executed.

One of the Calvinists, Jean de Léry, lived among the Tupinambá and later wrote a celebrated account of their customs, including ritual cannibalism, which Montaigne drew on for his essay “Of Cannibals”.

Governor-general Mem de Sá destroyed the fort in 1560, and his nephew Estácio de Sá founded a Portuguese town at the foot of the Sugarloaf on 1 March 1565. Estácio died of an arrow wound in the final battle of 1567, and the city of Rio was moved to a nearby hill.
story.zh:
马耳他骑士尼古拉·迪朗·德·维尔加尼翁说服海军上将科利尼和国王亨利二世支持在巴西建立殖民地，1555年在瓜纳巴拉湾的一座小岛上修建了科利尼堡。加尔文从日内瓦派来新教牧师，但关于圣餐的争论使殖民地分裂，维尔加尼翁处死了几名胡格诺派信徒。

加尔文派信徒让·德·莱里曾在图皮南巴人中生活，后来写下一部描述其风俗（包括仪式性食人）的著名记述，蒙田的随笔《论食人族》便参考了此书。

1560年总督门·德·萨摧毁了要塞，1565年3月1日他的侄子埃斯塔西奥·德·萨在面包山脚下建立葡萄牙城镇。1567年最后一战中埃斯塔西奥中箭身亡，里约城随后迁至附近山丘。

sources.title: Jean de Léry, Histoire d’un voyage fait en la terre du Brésil (1578)
Wikipedia: France Antarctique
Boris Fausto, A Concise History of Brazil (Cambridge UP, 1999)

name.en: Fall of Vilcabamba and execution of Túpac Amaru
name.zh: 比尔卡班巴陷落与图帕克·阿马鲁被处决

summary.en: Viceroy Francisco de Toledo used the killing of a Spanish envoy as pretext to invade the Neo-Inca State. His troops entered Vilcabamba in June 1572 and captured Túpac Amaru in the forest; the last Sapa Inca was beheaded in Cusco on 24 September 1572.
summary.zh: 总督弗朗西斯科·德·托莱多以一名西班牙使者被杀为借口入侵新印加国。1572年6月其军队进入比尔卡班巴，在森林中俘获图帕克·阿马鲁；同年9月24日，末代萨帕印卡在库斯科被斩首。

story.en:
Under Titu Cusi, Vilcabamba had negotiated with the Spanish, accepted Augustinian missionaries and dictated an account of the conquest from the Inca side. After Titu Cusi’s sudden death in 1571, his brother Túpac Amaru took power, and a Spanish messenger was killed at the frontier.

Toledo declared war. A force of Spaniards and thousands of Andean allies crossed the bridge at Chuquichaca and fought its way to Vilcabamba, which they found burned and abandoned on 24 June. A small party pursued Túpac Amaru down the rivers and captured him with his pregnant wife by a campfire.

In Cusco he was tried for rebellion and sentenced to death. Accounts describe a huge crowd wailing in the square until he raised his hand for silence. His death ended Inca sovereignty; Vilcabamba itself was forgotten until explorers rediscovered its ruins at Espíritu Pampa in the 20th century.
story.zh:
在蒂图·库西统治下，比尔卡班巴曾与西班牙人谈判，接纳奥斯定会传教士，并口述了一部从印加角度记录的征服史。1571年蒂图·库西猝死后，其弟图帕克·阿马鲁掌权，一名西班牙信使在边境被杀。

托莱多随即宣战。一支由西班牙人和数千安第斯盟军组成的部队越过丘基查卡桥，一路苦战抵达比尔卡班巴，6月24日发现城市已被焚毁、人去楼空。一支小分队沿河追击，在篝火旁俘获了图帕克·阿马鲁和他怀孕的妻子。

他在库斯科以叛乱罪受审并被判处死刑。据记载，广场上人山人海，哭声震天，直到他举手示意人群安静。他的死终结了印加主权；比尔卡班巴本身则被遗忘，直到20世纪探险者在埃斯皮里图潘帕重新发现其废墟。

sources.title: Baltasar de Ocampo, Descripción de la provincia de Vilcabamba (1610)
John Hemming, The Conquest of the Incas (1970)
Vincent R. Lee, Forgotten Vilcabamba (Sixpac Manco, 2000)

summary.en: Mapuche warriors under Pelantaro surprised Governor Martín García Óñez de Loyola’s camp at Curalaba at dawn and killed him with almost all his men. The victory sparked a general uprising that destroyed the seven Spanish cities south of the Biobío.
summary.zh: 佩兰塔罗率马普切战士黎明时分突袭库拉拉瓦的总督马丁·加西亚·奥涅斯·德·洛约拉营地，将其与几乎所有部下杀死。这场胜利引发大起义，比奥比奥河以南的七座西班牙城市尽被摧毁。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Battle of Curalaba
Diego de Rosales, Historia general del Reino de Chile (1674)
José Bengoa, Historia del pueblo mapuche (1985)

name.zh: 瓜拉尼人中的耶稣会传教区

summary.en: From 1609 Jesuits gathered Guaraní communities into some thirty mission towns along the Paraná and Uruguay rivers, with stone churches, workshops, cattle ranches and militias. At their peak in the 1730s they held about 140,000 people, until Charles III expelled the Jesuits in 1767.
summary.zh: 自1609年起，耶稣会士把瓜拉尼社群集中到巴拉那河与乌拉圭河沿岸约三十座传教镇中，镇上建有石砌教堂、作坊、牧场和民兵。18世纪30年代鼎盛时约有14万人，直到1767年查理三世驱逐耶稣会。

story.en:
The first reduction, San Ignacio Guazú, was founded in 1609. The Jesuits learned Guaraní, printed books in it and organised each town around a great plaza with the church on one side, the Guaraní families’ long houses on the others, and land worked both by families and in common.

The missions were exposed to slave raids by bandeirantes from São Paulo. In 1631 the Jesuit Antonio Ruiz de Montoya led some 12,000 people from the Guairá region down the Paraná to safety, and in 1641 Guaraní militias armed with firearms defeated a large raiding force at Mbororé.

Mission workshops produced violins, organs and printed books, and European visitors marvelled at the music of their choirs. After the expulsion of 1767 the towns declined, and their red sandstone ruins, such as São Miguel das Missões and Trinidad, are now World Heritage sites.
story.zh:
第一座传教区圣伊格纳西奥·瓜苏建于1609年。耶稣会士学习瓜拉尼语并用其印书，每座镇都围绕一个大广场布局：一侧是教堂，其余各侧是瓜拉尼家庭的长屋，土地既有家庭耕种的，也有共同耕作的。

传教区常遭圣保罗拓荒者的掳奴袭击。1631年耶稣会士安东尼奥·鲁伊斯·德·蒙托亚率约12000人从瓜伊拉地区沿巴拉那河南下避难；1641年配备火器的瓜拉尼民兵在姆博罗雷击败了一支大规模袭击队。

传教区作坊制作小提琴、管风琴和印刷书籍，欧洲访客惊叹于唱诗班的音乐。1767年驱逐令后各镇衰落，其红砂岩遗址如圣米格尔-达斯米松伊斯和特立尼达，如今已列为世界遗产。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Jesuit Missions of the Guaranis
Barbara Ganson, The Guaraní under Spanish Rule in the Río de la Plata (Stanford UP, 2003)
Antonio Ruiz de Montoya, Conquista espiritual (1639)

name.en: Guaman Poma finishes the Nueva corónica y buen gobierno
name.zh: 瓦曼·波马完成《新编年史与善政》

summary.en: Around 1615 the Andean noble Felipe Guaman Poma de Ayala completed a 1,189-page illustrated letter to Philip III describing Andean history and denouncing colonial abuse. Its 398 drawings are a unique Indigenous view of colonial Peru; the manuscript surfaced in Copenhagen in 1908.
summary.zh: 约1615年，安第斯贵族费利佩·瓦曼·波马·德·阿亚拉完成了一部致腓力三世、长达1189页的图文长信，叙述安第斯历史并控诉殖民暴政。书中398幅插图是原住民视角下殖民秘鲁的独特记录；手稿于1908年在哥本哈根被发现。

sources.title: Royal Danish Library, The Guaman Poma Website
Rolena Adorno, Guaman Poma: Writing and Resistance in Colonial Peru (University of Texas Press, 1986)

note: The manuscript is dated c. 1600–1615.

summary.en: In the forested hills of Alagoas, people who escaped the sugar plantations of Pernambuco built Palmares, a federation of fortified villages that lasted most of the 17th century. Ruled by kings such as Ganga Zumba and Zumbi, it withstood dozens of Dutch and Portuguese expeditions before falling in 1694.
summary.zh: 在阿拉戈斯的森林山地中，逃离伯南布哥甘蔗种植园的人们建立了帕尔马雷斯——一个由设防村落组成、存续了17世纪大部分时间的联盟。在甘加·尊巴和祖比等国王统治下，它抵御了数十次荷兰和葡萄牙的讨伐，1694年陷落。

story.en:
Runaways reached the Serra da Barriga from the early 1600s, and the turmoil of the Dutch war after 1630 let many more escape. By the later 17th century Palmares, which its people may have called Angola Janga, “little Angola”, comprised several large villages surrounded by palisades and fields of maize, beans and manioc.

Dutch expeditions of the 1640s left diaries describing streets, chapels and a council house in the main town. Its people included Africans of many origins, Brazilian-born Black people, Indigenous people and poor whites, and they traded with nearby settlers even while being attacked by them.

After the failed peace of 1678, Pernambuco hired Paulista bandeirantes. In early 1694 an army of several thousand with cannon besieged the capital, Macaco, for weeks before breaking in. Palmares became a symbol of Black resistance, and the Serra da Barriga is now a national memorial park.
story.zh:
17世纪初起便有逃亡者来到巴里加山，1630年后荷兰战争带来的动荡又使更多人得以逃脱。到17世纪后期，帕尔马雷斯——其居民或称之为“安哥拉·扬加”（小安哥拉）——已拥有数个被木栅环绕的大村落，周围种植玉米、豆类和木薯。

17世纪40年代荷兰讨伐队留下的日记描述了主镇的街道、小教堂和议事厅。居民中有来自非洲各地的人、生于巴西的黑人、原住民和贫苦白人；他们一边遭受附近定居者的攻击，一边仍与之贸易。

1678年和约破裂后，伯南布哥雇用圣保罗拓荒者。1694年初，一支数千人、配备火炮的军队围攻首都马卡科数周后破城。帕尔马雷斯成为黑人抵抗的象征，巴里加山如今是国家纪念公园。

sources.title: R. K. Kent, “Palmares: An African State in Brazil”, Journal of African History 6:2 (1965)
Flávio dos Santos Gomes, Palmares (Contexto, 2005)
Wikipedia: Palmares (quilombo)

note: The founding date is approximate; population estimates range from about 10,000 to 30,000.

summary.en: The Dutch West India Company captured Olinda and Recife in 1630 and held Brazil’s north-east sugar coast for 24 years. Governor Johan Maurits brought artists and naturalists; a Luso-Brazilian revolt from 1645, with victories at Guararapes, forced the Dutch to surrender Recife in 1654.
summary.zh: 1630年荷兰西印度公司攻占奥林达和累西腓，控制巴西东北部产糖海岸达24年。总督约翰·毛里茨带来了艺术家和博物学家；1645年起葡裔巴西人起义，在瓜拉拉皮斯获胜，迫使荷兰人于1654年交出累西腓。

label.zh: 荷兰人短暂占领萨尔瓦多（1624–1625）
攻占奥林达与累西腓
约翰·毛里茨抵达累西腓

label.en: Dutch seize Luanda to supply slaves
label.zh: 荷兰人夺取罗安达以供应奴隶
第一次瓜拉拉皮斯战役
荷兰人在累西腓投降

story.en:
The Dutch, at war with Spain and therefore with Portugal under the Spanish crown, wanted the world’s richest sugar lands. After a failed occupation of Salvador in 1624–25, a fleet took Pernambuco in 1630, and by 1641 the Company controlled much of the coast from Sergipe to Maranhão.

Johan Maurits of Nassau-Siegen, governor from 1637 to 1644, built the new town of Mauritsstad with bridges and gardens, tolerated Catholics and Jews, and brought the painters Frans Post and Albert Eckhout and the naturalists Georg Marcgrave and Willem Piso, whose Historia Naturalis Brasiliae (1648) was the first scientific survey of the country. Recife’s Kahal Zur Israel was the first synagogue in the Americas.

Planters indebted to the Company rose in 1645, and Luso-Brazilian, Indigenous and Afro-Brazilian troops defeated the Dutch twice at Guararapes. Recife surrendered in January 1654. Some of its Jewish families sailed north and helped found the Jewish community of New Amsterdam, later New York.
story.zh:
荷兰与西班牙交战，因而也与处于西班牙王室统治下的葡萄牙为敌，他们觊觎世界上最富庶的产糖之地。1624至1625年占领萨尔瓦多失败后，一支舰队于1630年攻取伯南布哥；到1641年，公司已控制从塞尔希培到马拉尼昂的大部分海岸。

1637至1644年任总督的拿骚-锡根的约翰·毛里茨兴建了有桥梁和花园的新城毛里茨斯塔德，宽容天主教徒和犹太人，并带来画家弗兰斯·波斯特、阿尔贝特·埃克豪特以及博物学家格奥尔格·马克格拉夫和威廉·皮索，后两人的《巴西自然史》（1648年）是对这片土地的首次科学考察。累西腓的“以色列之石”是美洲第一座犹太会堂。

1645年欠下公司债务的种植园主起事，葡裔巴西人、原住民和非裔巴西人组成的军队两度在瓜拉拉皮斯击败荷兰人。1654年1月累西腓投降。城中一些犹太家庭北上，参与建立了新阿姆斯特丹（后来的纽约）的犹太社区。

sources.title: C. R. Boxer, The Dutch in Brazil, 1624–1654 (Clarendon Press, 1957)
Evaldo Cabral de Mello, Olinda restaurada (1975)
Wikipedia: Dutch Brazil

summary.en: Governor Francisco López de Zúñiga, Marquis of Baides, met Mapuche leaders at Quilín and agreed a peace recognising the Biobío river as the frontier and Mapuche autonomy to its south, in exchange for freeing captives and admitting missionaries. Such parlamentos became the main tool of Spanish–Mapuche relations.
summary.zh: 总督巴伊德斯侯爵弗朗西斯科·洛佩斯·德·苏尼加在基林会见马普切首领，议定和约：承认比奥比奥河为边界及其以南马普切人的自治，马普切方面则释放俘虏并接纳传教士。此类议会成为西班牙与马普切关系的主要手段。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Parliament of Quillín
José Bengoa, Historia de los antiguos mapuches del sur (Catalonia, 2003)

note: Held on the plain of the Quillén river (Cautín province); the exact site is not known, so the marker sits on the river.

name.en: Brazilian gold rush in Minas Gerais

summary.en: Paulista bandeirantes found alluvial gold in the mountains of Minas Gerais in the 1690s, and diamonds followed in the 1720s. The rush drew Portuguese migrants and hundreds of thousands of enslaved Africans inland, built the baroque towns of Ouro Preto and Mariana, and moved the colonial capital to Rio in 1763.
summary.zh: 17世纪90年代，圣保罗拓荒者在米纳斯吉拉斯山区发现砂金，18世纪20年代又发现钻石。淘金热把葡萄牙移民和数十万被奴役的非洲人引向内陆，兴建了欧鲁普雷图、马里亚纳等巴洛克城镇，并促使殖民地首府于1763年迁往里约。

story.en:
After nearly two centuries of searching, bandeirantes struck gold in the rivers of the Serra do Espinhaço in the 1690s. News spread fast: Portuguese peasants emigrated in such numbers that the crown tried to restrict departures, and newcomers clashed with the Paulistas in the War of the Emboabas (1707–09).

Most of the digging was done by enslaved Africans, many brought from the Mina coast for their mining skills. The crown collected a royal fifth through foundry houses and later a head tax, and much of the gold flowed through Lisbon to British merchants under the Methuen Treaty of 1703.

Wealthy brotherhoods built the gilded churches of Vila Rica (Ouro Preto), where Aleijadinho worked. As output declined after the 1760s, tax demands sparked the Minas Conspiracy of 1789, whose leader Tiradentes was hanged in Rio in 1792.
story.zh:
经过近两个世纪的寻觅，拓荒者于17世纪90年代在埃斯皮尼亚苏山脉的河流中找到了黄金。消息迅速传开：葡萄牙农民大批移民，王室不得不设法限制出境；新来者与圣保罗人爆发了“外来者战争”（1707–1709年）。

采掘工作大多由被奴役的非洲人完成，其中许多人因善于采矿而从米纳海岸被运来。王室通过熔铸所征收“五一税”，后又改征人头税；大量黄金经里斯本流入英国商人手中，这得益于1703年的《梅休因条约》。

富有的宗教兄弟会在维拉里卡（欧鲁普雷图）修建了金碧辉煌的教堂，阿莱雅迪尼奥就在那里工作。18世纪60年代后产量下降，苛税引发了1789年的“米纳斯密谋”，其领袖蒂拉登特斯于1792年在里约被绞死。

sources.title: C. R. Boxer, The Golden Age of Brazil, 1695–1750 (University of California Press, 1962)
UNESCO World Heritage: Historic Town of Ouro Preto
Wikipedia: Brazilian Gold Rush

note: The rush is dated from the first strikes of 1693–95; output declined from the 1760s.

summary.en: In the War of Jenkins’ Ear, Admiral Edward Vernon attacked Cartagena with one of the largest fleets of the age, about 180 ships and some 25,000 men. The Spanish commander Blas de Lezo and Viceroy Eslava held the city’s forts for two months until disease forced the British to withdraw.
summary.zh: 詹金斯耳朵战争中，海军上将爱德华·弗农率当时规模最大的舰队之一（约180艘船、约2.5万人）进攻卡塔赫纳。西班牙指挥官布拉斯·德·莱索与总督埃斯拉瓦坚守城堡两个月，直到疫病迫使英军撤退。

story.en:
Vernon had taken Porto Bello in 1739 and London celebrated him as a hero. In March 1741 his fleet forced the narrow Bocachica entrance to Cartagena’s bay, and so confident was he that medals were struck in England showing Blas de Lezo kneeling before him.

Lezo, a veteran who had lost a leg, an eye and the use of an arm in earlier battles, scuttled ships to block the inner channel and fought on from the fortress of San Felipe de Barajas. A British night assault on the fortress in April failed when the scaling ladders proved too short.

Yellow fever and dysentery then killed thousands of British soldiers and sailors, among them many colonists from North America, including Lawrence Washington, who later named his Virginia estate Mount Vernon after the admiral. Lezo himself died of disease that September.
story.zh:
弗农于1739年攻下波托韦洛，伦敦视他为英雄。1741年3月，他的舰队强行突破卡塔赫纳海湾狭窄的博卡奇卡入口；他信心十足，英国甚至提前铸造了表现布拉斯·德·莱索向他下跪的纪念章。

莱索是一位老将，在以往战斗中失去了一条腿、一只眼和一只手臂的功能。他凿沉船只封锁内航道，在圣费利佩-德巴拉哈斯要塞继续抵抗。4月英军夜袭要塞，因云梯太短而失败。

随后黄热病和痢疾夺去了数千名英国官兵的生命，其中包括许多北美殖民地士兵，劳伦斯·华盛顿也在其中，他后来以这位海军上将之名，把自己在弗吉尼亚的庄园命名为弗农山庄。莱索本人于同年9月病逝。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Battle of Cartagena de Indias
Richard Harding, Amphibious Warfare in the Eighteenth Century: The British Expedition to the West Indies, 1740–1742 (Boydell, 1991)
UNESCO World Heritage: Port, Fortresses and Group of Monuments, Cartagena

name.zh: 利马—卡亚俄地震与海啸

summary.en: On the night of 28 October 1746 a great earthquake destroyed most of Lima, and a tsunami swept away the port of Callao, where only a few hundred of several thousand inhabitants survived. Viceroy Manso de Velasco led the rebuilding and was made Count of Superunda, “above the wave”.
summary.zh: 1746年10月28日夜，一场大地震摧毁了利马大部分地区，海啸卷走了卡亚俄港，数千居民中仅数百人幸存。总督曼索·德·贝拉斯科主持重建，获封“苏佩龙达伯爵”，意为“浪涛之上”。

story.en:
The shaking began around half past ten at night and lasted several minutes. Churches, the viceregal palace and thousands of adobe houses collapsed in Lima. Half an hour later the sea withdrew from Callao and returned as a wall of water that carried ships inland and left almost nothing of the town.

The viceroy, José Antonio Manso de Velasco, organised burials, food supplies and the rebuilding of the city. He tried to impose lower buildings and wider streets, and clashed with the Church and the elite over which churches and mansions could rise again.

Preachers blamed the disaster on Lima’s sins, and rumours of an Indigenous uprising followed in 1750. The historian Charles Walker has shown how the rebuilding became a battle over the Bourbon reforms in the viceroyalty.
story.zh:
震动约在夜里十点半开始，持续数分钟。利马的教堂、总督府和数以千计的土坯房屋倒塌。半小时后，卡亚俄的海水退去，随即化作一堵水墙扑回，把船只冲上陆地，城镇几乎荡然无存。

总督何塞·安东尼奥·曼索·德·贝拉斯科组织埋葬死者、供应粮食并重建城市。他试图推行低矮建筑和更宽的街道，在哪些教堂和宅邸可以重建的问题上与教会和精英发生冲突。

传教士把灾难归咎于利马的罪孽，1750年又传出原住民起义的谣言。历史学家查尔斯·沃克指出，这场重建演变成了围绕总督区波旁改革的斗争。

sources.title: Charles F. Walker, Shaky Colonialism: The 1746 Earthquake-Tsunami in Lima, Peru, and Its Long Aftermath (Duke UP, 2008)
Wikipedia: 1746 Lima–Callao earthquake

note: Death tolls vary widely; Lima lost at least a few thousand of about 60,000 inhabitants.

summary.en: The 1750 Treaty of Madrid gave Portugal seven Jesuit mission towns east of the Uruguay river in exchange for Colonia do Sacramento, and ordered some 30,000 Guaraní to leave. They resisted; a joint Spanish–Portuguese army crushed them at Caiboaté in February 1756.
summary.zh: 1750年《马德里条约》把乌拉圭河以东七座耶稣会传教镇割让给葡萄牙，以换取萨克拉门托殖民地，并命令约3万瓜拉尼人迁离。他们奋起抵抗，1756年2月西葡联军在凯博阿特将其击溃。

story.en:
The Seven Peoples of the Missions, including São Miguel and São Nicolau, were among the most prosperous reductions, with herds of cattle and fine churches. When surveyors arrived to mark the new border, the Guaraní refused to abandon their towns and their ancestors’ graves.

Their leader, the militia corregidor Sepé Tiaraju of São Miguel, is remembered for the cry “This land has an owner!”, a phrase later tradition attributes to him. He was killed in a skirmish on 7 February 1756, and three days later the allied army killed some 1,500 Guaraní at Caiboaté with few losses of its own.

The treaty was annulled in 1761, but the war fed the campaign against the Jesuits, who were expelled from Portugal’s domains in 1759 and Spain’s in 1767. The story inspired the film The Mission (1986).
story.zh:
包括圣米格尔和圣尼古拉在内的“传教区七镇”是最富庶的传教区之一，拥有成群的牛和精美的教堂。勘界人员前来标定新边界时，瓜拉尼人拒绝离开自己的城镇和祖先的坟墓。

他们的首领、圣米格尔的民兵长官塞佩·蒂亚拉茹，以一句“这片土地是有主人的！”而为人铭记（这句话是后世传统归于他的）。1756年2月7日他在一次小规模战斗中阵亡，三天后联军在凯博阿特杀死约1500名瓜拉尼人，自身损失甚微。

条约于1761年被废除，但这场战争助长了反耶稣会运动，耶稣会于1759年被逐出葡萄牙领地，1767年被逐出西班牙领地。电影《教会》（1986年）即取材于此。

sources.title: Barbara Ganson, The Guaraní under Spanish Rule in the Río de la Plata (Stanford UP, 2003)
Wikipedia: Guaraní War
Tau Golin, A Guerra Guaranítica (Editora da UPF, 1998)

name.zh: 图帕克·阿马鲁二世起义

summary.en: Beginning with the execution of a corregidor at Tinta in November 1780, the rebellion spread across the southern Andes against forced labour, forced sales and Bourbon taxes. Its leaders were executed in Cusco in 1781, but fighting continued under Túpac Katari, who besieged La Paz, until 1783.
summary.zh: 起义始于1780年11月廷塔一名地方长官被处决，随后席卷安第斯南部，反对强制劳役、强制摊售和波旁赋税。起义领袖于1781年在库斯科被处决，但战斗在围攻拉巴斯的图帕克·卡塔里领导下持续到1783年。

label.zh: 廷塔：长官阿里亚加被绞死（11月10日）
桑加拉拉大捷（11月18日）
围攻库斯科失败（1月）
图帕克·阿马鲁在兰圭附近被俘（4月）
图帕克·卡塔里围攻拉巴斯

label.en: Last rebel leaders surrender in the Titicaca basin
label.zh: 最后的起义首领在的的喀喀湖盆地投降

story.en:
By the 1770s the reparto, the forced sale of mules and cloth by provincial officials, and new Bourbon taxes weighed heavily on Andean communities. Rebellion had already broken out in Chayanta in Upper Peru when José Gabriel Condorcanqui, as Túpac Amaru II, seized the corregidor of Tinta.

The movement drew Indigenous people, mestizos and some creoles, and at first claimed loyalty to the king against bad officials. After Túpac Amaru’s capture, his cousin Diego Cristóbal and the Aymara leader Julián Apaza, known as Túpac Katari, carried it on. With his wife Bartolina Sisa, Túpac Katari twice besieged La Paz in 1781, first for 109 days from March and again from August to October.

Repression was ferocious, and perhaps 100,000 people died. The crown abolished the hereditary Indigenous chieftainships tied to the rebellion and banned Inca dress, portraits and Garcilaso’s Comentarios Reales in Peru.
story.zh:
到18世纪70年代，地方官员强制摊售骡子和布匹的“摊派制”以及新的波旁赋税沉重地压在安第斯社群身上。上秘鲁的查扬塔已爆发起义，此时何塞·加夫列尔·孔多尔坎基以图帕克·阿马鲁二世之名扣押了廷塔的地方长官。

运动吸引了原住民、混血人和部分土生白人，起初还声称效忠国王、反对贪官。图帕克·阿马鲁被俘后，他的堂弟迭戈·克里斯托瓦尔和艾马拉首领胡利安·阿帕萨（人称图帕克·卡塔里）继续斗争。1781年图帕克·卡塔里与妻子巴托利娜·西萨两度围攻拉巴斯：第一次自3月起持续109天，第二次从8月持续到10月。

镇压极其残酷，死亡人数或达十万。王室废除了与起义相关的世袭原住民首领制度，并在秘鲁禁止印加服饰、画像和加西拉索的《印卡王室述评》。

sources.title: Charles F. Walker, The Tupac Amaru Rebellion (Harvard UP, 2014)
Sinclair Thomson, We Alone Will Rule: Native Andean Politics in the Age of Insurgency (University of Wisconsin Press, 2002)
Britannica: Túpac Amaru II

summary.en: Poets, priests, officers and mine owners of Vila Rica, inspired by the American Revolution, plotted to make Minas Gerais an independent republic when a hated gold tax was due. Betrayed in 1789, the conspirators were exiled; only the ensign Tiradentes was hanged, in Rio on 21 April 1792.
summary.zh: 受美国革命鼓舞，维拉里卡的诗人、神父、军官和矿主在一项令人痛恨的黄金税到期之际密谋使米纳斯吉拉斯成为独立共和国。1789年密谋被告发，参与者遭流放；只有少尉蒂拉登特斯于1792年4月21日在里约被绞死。

sources.title: Kenneth Maxwell, Conflicts and Conspiracies: Brazil and Portugal, 1750–1808 (Cambridge UP, 1973)
Wikipedia: Inconfidência Mineira

name.en: Humboldt and Bonpland’s American expedition and the Chimborazo climb
name.zh: 洪堡与邦普朗的美洲考察及攀登钦博拉索山

summary.en: During their five-year expedition through Spanish America, Alexander von Humboldt and Aimé Bonpland climbed to about 5,900 m on Chimborazo, then thought the highest mountain on Earth. Humboldt’s cross-section of the volcano, published in 1807, showed plant life changing with altitude and founded biogeography.
summary.zh: 在历时五年的西属美洲考察中，亚历山大·冯·洪堡与艾梅·邦普朗攀登到钦博拉索山约5900米处，当时人们认为这是地球最高峰。洪堡于1807年发表的火山剖面图展示了植物随海拔变化的规律，奠定了生物地理学。

label.zh: 在库马纳登陆（7月）
在卡拉沃索附近研究电鳗

label.en: Confirm the Casiquiare link between Orinoco and Amazon
label.zh: 证实卡西基亚雷河连通奥里诺科河与亚马孙河

label.en: Visit José Celestino Mutis in Bogotá
label.zh: 在波哥大拜访何塞·塞莱斯蒂诺·穆蒂斯
攀登基多周边的火山
攀登钦博拉索山（6月23日）

label.en: Observe the transit of Mercury at Callao
label.zh: 在卡亚俄观测水星凌日
自瓜亚基尔启航前往阿卡普尔科（2月）
在波尔多返回欧洲（8月）

story.en:
Humboldt, a wealthy Prussian with a passion for measurement, received unusual permission from the Spanish crown to travel through its American colonies. With the French botanist Bonpland he paddled the Orinoco, measured the electric shocks of eels that stunned horses in the llanos, and confirmed that the Casiquiare river joins the Orinoco and Amazon basins.

On 23 June 1802, with Bonpland, the young Ecuadorian Carlos Montúfar and local helpers, he climbed Chimborazo through snow and cloud, suffering nausea and bleeding gums, until a deep ravine stopped them at around 5,900 metres. It was the highest any European was known to have climbed, a record he was proud of for the rest of his life.

Back in Europe he drew the Naturgemälde, a cross-section of Chimborazo labelled with the plants found at each height, and argued that nature is a web of connected forces. Simón Bolívar, who met him in Paris, later called him the true discoverer of America.
story.zh:
洪堡是一位热衷于测量的富有普鲁士人，罕见地获得西班牙王室许可，游历其美洲殖民地。他与法国植物学家邦普朗划船沿奥里诺科河而上，测量了在平原上电晕马匹的电鳗，并证实卡西基亚雷河把奥里诺科河与亚马孙河两大流域连在一起。

1802年6月23日，他与邦普朗、年轻的厄瓜多尔人卡洛斯·蒙图法尔及当地向导冒着风雪云雾攀登钦博拉索山，忍受着恶心和牙龈出血，直到一道深谷在约5900米处挡住去路。这是当时已知欧洲人攀登的最高海拔，他终生以此为傲。

回到欧洲后，他绘制了“自然之图”——钦博拉索山剖面图，标注出各个高度的植物，并主张自然是一张由相互关联的力量编织的网。在巴黎与他相识的西蒙·玻利瓦尔后来称他为美洲真正的发现者。

sources.title: Alexander von Humboldt & Aimé Bonpland, Essai sur la géographie des plantes (1807)
Andrea Wulf, The Invention of Nature: Alexander von Humboldt’s New World (Knopf, 2015)
Britannica: Alexander von Humboldt

note: The expedition ran from June 1799 (departure from A Coruña) to August 1804; the Chimborazo climb was on 23 June 1802. Humboldt gave his highest point as 3,036 toises (about 5,917 m); modern estimates are somewhat lower.

summary.en: As Napoleon’s army approached Lisbon, Prince Regent John, the mad Queen Maria I and some 10,000–15,000 courtiers sailed for Brazil under British escort. They reached Salvador in January 1808 and Rio in March, opening Brazil’s ports to foreign trade and turning Rio into the capital of a global monarchy.
summary.zh: 拿破仑大军逼近里斯本之际，摄政王若昂、患精神病的女王玛丽亚一世及约1万至1.5万名朝臣在英国护航下驶往巴西。他们于1808年1月抵达萨尔瓦多，3月抵达里约，向外国开放巴西港口，使里约成为一个全球性君主国的首都。

label.zh: 船队离开里斯本（11月29日）
抵达萨尔瓦多，开放港口（1月）
王室在里约登岸（3月）

story.en:
In November 1807 General Junot’s French army marched on Lisbon to force Portugal into Napoleon’s blockade of Britain. Prince John chose to leave rather than submit: in a few chaotic days the court packed archives, the royal library and the treasury onto dozens of ships, and the fleet sailed on 29 November as the French entered the outskirts.

After a stormy crossing the royal family landed at Salvador, where John decreed the opening of Brazil’s ports to friendly nations, ending three centuries of monopoly. In Rio, residents were evicted from their houses to lodge the courtiers, whose doors were marked “P.R.” for Príncipe Regente, which locals mocked as “ponha-se na rua”, “get out into the street”.

The court founded a bank, a printing press, a military academy, a botanical garden and a royal library in Rio. In 1815 Brazil became a kingdom equal to Portugal, and when John returned to Lisbon in 1821 he left his son Pedro behind.
story.zh:
1807年11月，朱诺将军率法军进军里斯本，逼迫葡萄牙加入拿破仑对英国的封锁。若昂亲王宁可出走也不屈服：在混乱的几天里，朝廷把档案、王家图书馆和国库装上数十艘船，11月29日法军进入郊区之际船队启航。

经过风暴中的横渡，王室在萨尔瓦多登岸，若昂在此颁布法令向友好国家开放巴西港口，结束了三个世纪的贸易垄断。在里约，居民被赶出房屋以安置朝臣，门上标着代表“摄政王”的“P.R.”字样，当地人戏称其意为“滚到街上去”。

王室在里约设立了银行、印刷所、军事学院、植物园和王家图书馆。1815年巴西升格为与葡萄牙平等的王国；1821年若昂返回里斯本时，把儿子佩德罗留在了巴西。

sources.title: Kirsten Schultz, Tropical Versailles: Empire, Monarchy, and the Portuguese Royal Court in Rio de Janeiro, 1808–1821 (Routledge, 2001)
Laurentino Gomes, 1808 (Planeta, 2007)
Wikipedia: Transfer of the Portuguese Court to Brazil

note: Estimates of the number who sailed range from about 10,000 to 15,000.

name.zh: 布宜诺斯艾利斯五月革命

summary.en: When news arrived that the Spanish junta in Seville had fallen to Napoleon, Buenos Aires creoles called an open town council, deposed Viceroy Cisneros and on 25 May 1810 installed the Primera Junta. Though it still ruled in Ferdinand VII’s name, the May Revolution began Argentina’s independence.
summary.zh: 塞维利亚的西班牙洪达落入拿破仑之手的消息传来后，布宜诺斯艾利斯的土生白人召开公开市政会议，废黜总督西斯内罗斯，于1810年5月25日成立第一洪达。尽管它仍以斐迪南七世的名义执政，五月革命开启了阿根廷的独立进程。

story.en:
Buenos Aires had already shown its strength in 1806 and 1807, when local militias rather than Spanish troops drove off two British invasions. When Napoleon took Spain and imprisoned Ferdinand VII, the question was who now held authority in America.

A British ship brought news in mid-May 1810 that the central junta in Seville had collapsed. Militia commanders led by Cornelio Saavedra refused to defend the viceroy, and on 22 May an open cabildo of leading residents voted to remove him. After a failed attempt to keep Cisneros at the head of a new junta, crowds gathered outside the cabildo on 25 May and a nine-member Primera Junta took power, with Saavedra as president and Mariano Moreno as secretary.

The Junta sent armies to Upper Peru, Paraguay and the Banda Oriental. Formal independence came only at Tucumán in 1816, but 25 May is celebrated as Argentina’s national day.
story.zh:
1806年和1807年，正是本地民兵而非西班牙军队击退了英国的两次入侵，布宜诺斯艾利斯已显示出自身的力量。拿破仑占领西班牙并囚禁斐迪南七世后，问题变成了：如今在美洲由谁掌权？

1810年5月中旬，一艘英国船带来塞维利亚中央洪达垮台的消息。以科尔内略·萨韦德拉为首的民兵指挥官拒绝保卫总督，5月22日，由城中显要组成的公开市政会议投票罢免了他。在保留西斯内罗斯领导新洪达的企图失败后，5月25日人群聚集在市政厅外，一个九人组成的第一洪达掌权，萨韦德拉任主席，马里亚诺·莫雷诺任秘书。

洪达派军队前往上秘鲁、巴拉圭和东岸地区。正式独立直到1816年才在图库曼宣布，但5月25日被定为阿根廷国庆日。

sources.title: Britannica: May Revolution
Tulio Halperín Donghi, Politics, Economics and Society in Argentina in the Revolutionary Period (Cambridge UP, 1975)
John Lynch, The Spanish American Revolutions, 1808–1826 (2nd ed., 1986)

summary.en: On 5 July 1811 the congress of the Venezuelan provinces, meeting in Caracas, declared absolute independence from Spain, the first Spanish American territory to do so. The First Republic collapsed a year later after the earthquake of March 1812 and royalist counter-attacks.
summary.zh: 1811年7月5日，委内瑞拉各省议会在加拉加斯宣布完全脱离西班牙独立，这是西属美洲第一个这样做的地区。一年后，在1812年3月地震和保王派反攻之下，第一共和国崩溃。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Venezuelan Declaration of Independence
John Lynch, Simón Bolívar: A Life (Yale UP, 2006)

summary.en: Delegates of the United Provinces of South America, meeting in a colonial house in San Miguel de Tucumán, declared independence from Spain and “any other foreign domination” on 9 July 1816, while San Martín prepared his army in Mendoza.
summary.zh: 1816年7月9日，南美洲联合省的代表在圣米格尔-德图库曼一座殖民时期的宅邸中宣布脱离西班牙及“任何其他外国统治”而独立，此时圣马丁正在门多萨整军备战。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Argentine Declaration of Independence
David Rock, Argentina 1516–1987 (University of California Press, 1987)

name.en: Crossing of the Andes and Battle of Chacabuco
name.zh: 翻越安第斯山与查卡布科战役

summary.en: In January 1817 San Martín’s Army of the Andes, about 5,000 men with thousands of mules and horses, crossed the cordillera in several columns through passes above 4,000 m. On 12 February it routed the royalists at Chacabuco and entered Santiago, freeing central Chile.
summary.zh: 1817年1月，圣马丁的安第斯军约五千人，携带数千头骡马，分几路经海拔四千米以上的山口翻越安第斯山脉。2月12日在查卡布科击溃保王军，进入圣地亚哥，解放了智利中部。
