拉斯埃拉斯纵队经乌斯帕利亚塔

label.en: Main body over the Los Patos pass
label.zh: 主力翻越洛斯帕托斯山口
下到阿空加瓜河谷
查卡布科大捷（2月12日）
进入圣地亚哥

story.en:
San Martín spent three years turning the province of Cuyo into an arsenal. The friar Luis Beltrán ran a foundry that cast cannon and horseshoes, women of Mendoza sewed uniforms, and slaves freed for service made up a large part of the infantry. Spies spread false reports about which passes the army would use.

The army set off in January 1817 with some 10,000 mules and 1,600 horses, food for a month and portable bridges. Six columns crossed along a front hundreds of kilometres wide so the royalists could not concentrate; the main body under San Martín and O’Higgins took the Los Patos route, where many animals died from cold and altitude.

At Chacabuco on 12 February, O’Higgins charged ahead of the planned attack and the royalists broke, losing about 500 dead and 600 prisoners. Santiago was taken two days later, and Chile declared its independence a year later.
story.zh:
圣马丁用三年时间把库约省变成了兵工厂。路易斯·贝尔特兰修士主持铸造厂，铸造火炮和马蹄铁；门多萨的妇女缝制军装；因参军而获释的奴隶构成步兵的很大部分。间谍四处散布假情报，混淆军队将经过哪些山口。

1817年1月大军出发，带着约一万头骡子、1600匹马、一个月的口粮和便携桥梁。六路纵队在宽达数百公里的战线上同时翻越，使保王军无法集中兵力；圣马丁和奥希金斯率主力走洛斯帕托斯路线，许多牲畜死于严寒和高原反应。

2月12日在查卡布科，奥希金斯抢在预定时间之前发起冲锋，保王军溃败，约500人战死、600人被俘。两天后攻占圣地亚哥，一年后智利宣布独立。

sources.title: John Lynch, San Martín: Argentine Soldier, American Hero (Yale UP, 2009)
Bartolomé Mitre, Historia de San Martín y de la emancipación sudamericana (1887–88)
Wikipedia: Crossing of the Andes

summary.en: Weeks after a surprise defeat at Cancha Rayada, San Martín’s Chilean–Argentine army destroyed the royalist expedition from Peru on the plains of Maipú near Santiago, securing Chile’s independence. The embrace of San Martín and the wounded O’Higgins on the field became a national icon.
summary.zh: 在坎查拉亚达遭突袭失利数周后，圣马丁的智利—阿根廷联军在圣地亚哥附近的迈普平原歼灭了从秘鲁来犯的保王军，确保了智利独立。圣马丁与负伤的奥希金斯在战场上的拥抱成为国家象征。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Battle of Maipú
Simon Collier & William F. Sater, A History of Chile, 1808–2002 (2004)

summary.en: Meeting in the Orinoco river town of Angostura, Bolívar’s congress heard his famous address on republican government and in December 1819 proclaimed the Republic of Colombia, uniting Venezuela and New Granada.
summary.zh: 玻利瓦尔召集的国会在奥里诺科河畔的安戈斯图拉召开，聆听了他关于共和政体的著名演说，并于1819年12月宣告成立哥伦比亚共和国，统合委内瑞拉与新格拉纳达。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Congress of Angostura
Simón Bolívar, Discurso de Angostura (15 February 1819)

name.en: Bolívar’s Andean campaign and the Battle of Boyacá
name.zh: 玻利瓦尔的安第斯远征与博亚卡战役

summary.en: In the rainy season of 1819 Bolívar led some 2,500 men across the flooded llanos and over the freezing Páramo de Pisba into New Granada. At the bridge of Boyacá on 7 August he defeated and captured the royalist army; the viceroy fled Bogotá, which Bolívar entered three days later.
summary.zh: 1819年雨季，玻利瓦尔率约2500人穿越被洪水淹没的平原，翻越冰冷的皮斯巴高原进入新格拉纳达。8月7日在博亚卡桥击败并俘获保王军；总督逃离波哥大，三天后玻利瓦尔入城。

label.en: Leaves Mantecal in the Apure llanos (May)
label.zh: 从阿普雷平原的曼特卡尔出发（5月）
在塔梅与桑坦德军会合（6月）

label.en: Crosses the Páramo de Pisba (early July)
label.zh: 翻越皮斯巴高原（7月初）

label.en: Battle of the Pantano de Vargas (25 July)
label.zh: 巴尔加斯沼泽之战（7月25日）

label.en: Victory at the Boyacá bridge (7 August)
label.zh: 博亚卡桥大捷（8月7日）
进入波哥大（8月10日）

story.en:
Bolívar’s plan was audacious: instead of attacking the royalists in Venezuela, he would strike New Granada from the east, where no one expected an army in the rainy season. His troops, llaneros and British volunteers, waded for weeks across plains turned into lakes, then climbed into the Andes through the Páramo de Pisba, where many barefoot men died of cold.

The royalist commander José María Barreiro met them at the Pantano de Vargas on 25 July. When the patriots were near defeat, the llanero colonel Juan José Rondón led a cavalry charge that saved the day, an episode later told with Bolívar’s legendary words, “Colonel, save the fatherland!”.

On 7 August Bolívar caught Barreiro’s army crossing the Boyacá bridge and captured him with most of his men in two hours. Viceroy Sámano fled Bogotá in disguise, leaving the treasury behind, and the victory opened the way to Gran Colombia.
story.zh:
玻利瓦尔的计划极为大胆：他不在委内瑞拉进攻保王军，而是从东面突袭新格拉纳达，没有人料到雨季会有军队从那里出现。他的部队由平原骑兵和英国志愿兵组成，在变成湖泊的平原上跋涉数周，再经皮斯巴高原登上安第斯山，许多赤脚士兵冻死途中。

7月25日，保王军指挥官何塞·玛丽亚·巴雷罗在巴尔加斯沼泽迎战。爱国军濒临失败时，平原骑兵上校胡安·何塞·龙东率骑兵冲锋扭转战局，后来流传的故事中还配上了玻利瓦尔的传奇话语：“上校，拯救祖国吧！”

8月7日，玻利瓦尔在巴雷罗的军队渡过博亚卡桥时将其截住，两小时内俘获巴雷罗及其大部分部下。总督萨马诺乔装逃离波哥大，连国库都丢下了。这场胜利为大哥伦比亚的建立铺平了道路。

sources.title: Britannica: Battle of Boyacá
John Lynch, Simón Bolívar: A Life (Yale UP, 2006)
Daniel Florence O’Leary, Memorias del general O’Leary (1879–88)

summary.en: Bolívar’s army outflanked the royalists on the plain of Carabobo, west of Valencia, with Páez’s llanero cavalry and the British Legion bearing the brunt. The victory freed Caracas and effectively ended Spanish rule in Venezuela.
summary.zh: 玻利瓦尔的军队在巴伦西亚以西的卡拉沃沃平原迂回包抄保王军，派斯的平原骑兵和英国军团首当其冲。这场胜利解放了加拉加斯，实际上结束了西班牙在委内瑞拉的统治。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Battle of Carabobo
John Lynch, Simón Bolívar: A Life (Yale UP, 2006)

summary.en: Antonio José de Sucre’s army of Colombians, Peruvians and Argentines climbed the slopes of the Pichincha volcano overnight and defeated the royalists above Quito at about 3,500 m. The victory freed the Audiencia of Quito, which joined Gran Colombia.
summary.zh: 安东尼奥·何塞·德·苏克雷率领由哥伦比亚人、秘鲁人和阿根廷人组成的军队连夜攀上皮钦查火山山坡，在基多上方约3500米处击败保王军。这场胜利解放了基多检审庭辖区，该地随后并入大哥伦比亚。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Battle of Pichincha
John Lynch, The Spanish American Revolutions, 1808–1826 (1986)

summary.en: The two liberators, Bolívar and San Martín, met privately for two days in Guayaquil. No record of their talks survives; afterwards San Martín resigned his command in Peru and withdrew from the war, leaving Bolívar to finish it; he later left for Europe.
summary.zh: 两位解放者玻利瓦尔与圣马丁在瓜亚基尔秘密会谈两天，谈话内容没有留下记录。此后圣马丁辞去在秘鲁的指挥权并退出战争，由玻利瓦尔完成解放；他后来远走欧洲。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Guayaquil Conference
John Lynch, San Martín: Argentine Soldier, American Hero (Yale UP, 2009)

name.en: Independence of Brazil: the Cry of Ipiranga
name.zh: 巴西独立：伊皮兰加呐喊

summary.en: Ordered by the Lisbon Cortes to return to Portugal, Prince Regent Pedro refused and, on the banks of the Ipiranga stream near São Paulo on 7 September 1822, declared Brazil independent with the cry “Independence or death!”. He was crowned emperor in Rio on 1 December.
summary.zh: 里斯本议会命令摄政王佩德罗返回葡萄牙，他拒绝服从，并于1822年9月7日在圣保罗附近的伊皮兰加溪畔高呼“不独立，毋宁死！”宣布巴西独立。12月1日他在里约加冕为皇帝。

story.en:
After King John VI returned to Lisbon in 1821, the Portuguese parliament set out to reduce Brazil to a colony again and ordered Pedro home. On 9 January 1822, presented with a petition of 8,000 signatures, he declared that he would stay, a day Brazilians remember as the Dia do Fico.

In September Pedro was travelling back from Santos to São Paulo when a messenger caught up with him by the Ipiranga stream with letters from Lisbon annulling his decrees, and from his wife Leopoldina and his minister José Bonifácio urging a break. According to witnesses he tore the Portuguese colours from his uniform and shouted “Independence or death!”.

Portuguese garrisons in Bahia, Maranhão and Pará held out until 1823, and Portugal recognised independence in 1825 in exchange for compensation. Pedro Américo’s grand painting of the scene, made in 1888, gave it a splendour the muddy roadside probably lacked.
story.zh:
1821年国王若昂六世返回里斯本后，葡萄牙议会着手把巴西重新降为殖民地，并命令佩德罗回国。1822年1月9日，面对一份有八千人签名的请愿书，他宣布留下，巴西人称这一天为“我留下日”。

9月，佩德罗从桑托斯返回圣保罗途中，一名信使在伊皮兰加溪畔追上他，送来里斯本宣布废除其法令的公文，以及妻子莱奥波尔迪娜和大臣若泽·博尼法西奥敦促决裂的信件。据目击者说，他扯下军服上的葡萄牙徽饰，高呼“不独立，毋宁死！”

巴伊亚、马拉尼昂和帕拉的葡萄牙驻军一直坚持到1823年，葡萄牙在获得赔偿后于1825年承认巴西独立。佩德罗·阿梅里科1888年创作的宏大画作赋予了这一场景一种那条泥泞路边或许并不具备的辉煌。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Independence of Brazil
Neill Macaulay, Dom Pedro: The Struggle for Liberty in Brazil and Portugal, 1798–1834 (Duke UP, 1986)
Lilia M. Schwarcz & Heloisa M. Starling, Brazil: A Biography (2018)

summary.en: On the plain of Quinua near Ayacucho, Sucre’s army of about 6,000 defeated a larger royalist force and captured Viceroy José de la Serna. The capitulation signed the same day ended the Spanish empire in South America, though small garrisons held out until 1826.
summary.zh: 在阿亚库乔附近的基努阿平原，苏克雷率约六千人击败兵力更多的保王军，俘获总督何塞·德·拉塞尔纳。当天签署的投降书终结了西班牙在南美的帝国，尽管少数守军坚持到1826年。

story.en:
After Bolívar’s cavalry won at Junín in August 1824, the royalist army in the highlands, Spain’s last field army in the continent, tried to cut off Sucre. The two armies manoeuvred for weeks through the mountains before meeting on the high plain of Quinua on 9 December.

The royalists attacked downhill from the slopes of the Condorcunca. The Colombian general José María Córdova led his division forward with the order “Weapons at will, march with the step of conquerors!” and broke the royalist centre. The wounded viceroy La Serna was taken prisoner, and by afternoon his general Canterac had signed a capitulation that also surrendered Peru.

Sucre was named Grand Marshal of Ayacucho. The fortress of Callao held out until January 1826, but the battle is remembered as the end of three centuries of Spanish rule.
story.zh:
1824年8月玻利瓦尔的骑兵在胡宁获胜后，盘踞高原的保王军——西班牙在南美大陆的最后一支野战军——企图截断苏克雷。两军在山地中周旋数周，12月9日在基努阿高原相遇。

保王军从孔多尔昆卡山坡向下进攻。哥伦比亚将军何塞·玛丽亚·科尔多瓦率师前进，下令“随意持枪，以征服者的步伐前进！”，突破了保王军中路。负伤的总督拉塞尔纳被俘，到下午他的将领坎特拉克签署了投降书，连同整个秘鲁一并交出。

苏克雷被授予“阿亚库乔大元帅”称号。卡亚俄要塞坚持到1826年1月，但这场战役被视为西班牙三个世纪统治的终结。

sources.title: Britannica: Battle of Ayacucho
John Lynch, The Spanish American Revolutions, 1808–1826 (1986)
Timothy E. Anna, The Fall of the Royal Government in Peru (University of Nebraska Press, 1979)

summary.en: HMS Beagle under Robert FitzRoy spent nearly five years surveying South America’s coasts, carrying the young naturalist Charles Darwin. His fossils from Argentina, the 1835 Chilean earthquake, the Andes and the Galápagos fed the ideas he published in 1859 as On the Origin of Species.
summary.zh: 罗伯特·菲茨罗伊指挥的“小猎犬号”用近五年时间测绘南美海岸，船上载着年轻的博物学家查尔斯·达尔文。他在阿根廷发现的化石、1835年智利地震、安第斯山和加拉帕戈斯群岛的见闻，孕育了他1859年发表于《物种起源》中的思想。

label.zh: 自普利茅斯出发（12月27日）

label.en: Salvador da Bahia: Darwin’s first rainforest
label.zh: 巴伊亚萨尔瓦多：达尔文初见热带雨林
里约热内卢

label.en: Fossils of giant mammals at Punta Alta
label.zh: 在蓬塔阿尔塔发现巨型哺乳动物化石

label.en: Returns Fuegian passengers in the Beagle Channel
label.zh: 在比格尔海峡送回火地岛乘客
瓦尔帕莱索与安第斯山

label.en: Witnesses the great earthquake at Valdivia (20 February)
label.zh: 在瓦尔迪维亚亲历大地震（2月20日）
加拉帕戈斯群岛（9–10月）
回到法尔茅斯（10月2日）

story.en:
The Admiralty sent the Beagle to chart the coasts of South America for navigation. Its 26-year-old captain, Robert FitzRoy, wanted a gentleman companion who could collect specimens, and the place went to Charles Darwin, 22, fresh from Cambridge. FitzRoy also brought back three Fuegians he had taken to England on an earlier voyage, among them a young man the sailors called Jemmy Button.

Darwin was seasick for most of the voyage and spent much of it on land, riding with gauchos across the pampas and climbing the Andes. At Punta Alta in 1832 he dug up the bones of giant extinct mammals related to living armadillos and sloths. In February 1835 he felt the earthquake that ruined Concepción and saw that the coast had risen by about a metre, and high in the Andes he found fossil seashells.

In the Galápagos he noticed that mockingbirds differed from island to island. Back in England these observations led him to doubt that species were fixed; he published his Journal of Researches in 1839 and On the Origin of Species in 1859.
story.zh:
海军部派“小猎犬号”测绘南美海岸以利航行。26岁的舰长罗伯特·菲茨罗伊希望有一位能采集标本的绅士旅伴，这个位置给了刚从剑桥毕业、22岁的查尔斯·达尔文。菲茨罗伊还把上次航行带往英国的三名火地岛人送回故乡，其中一位年轻人被水手们称为“杰米·巴顿”。

达尔文在航程中大部分时间晕船，因此常在陆地上活动：与高乔人一起骑马穿越潘帕斯草原，攀登安第斯山。1832年他在蓬塔阿尔塔挖出与现生犰狳、树懒有亲缘关系的已灭绝巨型哺乳动物骨骼。1835年2月他亲历了摧毁康塞普西翁的地震，看到海岸抬升了约一米；在安第斯山高处，他又发现了贝壳化石。

在加拉帕戈斯群岛，他注意到各岛的嘲鸫互不相同。回到英国后，这些观察使他怀疑物种是否固定不变；他于1839年出版《考察日记》，1859年出版《物种起源》。

name.en: Paraguayan War (War of the Triple Alliance)
name.zh: 巴拉圭战争（三国同盟战争）

summary.en: Paraguay’s Francisco Solano López attacked Brazil’s Mato Grosso and then Argentine Corrientes, bringing Brazil, Argentina and Uruguay into alliance against him. The longest and deadliest interstate war in South American history destroyed Paraguay, which lost a large share of its population and territory.
summary.zh: 巴拉圭的弗朗西斯科·索拉诺·洛佩斯先后进攻巴西马托格罗索和阿根廷科连特斯，促使巴西、阿根廷和乌拉圭结盟对抗。这是南美历史上历时最长、伤亡最惨重的国家间战争，巴拉圭损失了大量人口和领土，几近覆灭。

label.zh: 巴拉圭入侵马托格罗索（12月）

label.en: Brazilian naval victory at Riachuelo (11 June)
label.zh: 巴西海军在里亚丘埃洛获胜（6月11日）
巴拉圭军在乌拉圭亚纳投降

label.en: Battle of Tuyutí, the largest in South American history (24 May)
label.zh: 图尤蒂战役，南美史上规模最大的战役（5月24日）
盟军在库鲁派蒂惨败（9月22日）
乌迈塔要塞陷落
盟军占领亚松森（1月）

label.en: López killed at Cerro Corá (1 March)
label.zh: 洛佩斯在塞罗科拉阵亡（3月1日）

story.en:
Solano López had inherited a centralised state with an army of perhaps 60,000–70,000 men, the largest in the region. When Brazil intervened in Uruguay’s civil war in 1864, he seized a Brazilian steamer and invaded Mato Grosso; Argentina’s refusal to let his troops cross Corrientes brought it into the war, and on 1 May 1865 the Treaty of the Triple Alliance bound the allies to fight until López was removed.

The war bogged down around the fortress of Humaitá, which guarded the Paraguay river. At Curupayty in September 1866 the allies lost thousands of men in a frontal assault, while cholera ravaged both sides. Brazil, which bore most of the burden, sent its new ironclads past Humaitá in 1868.

López retreated into the interior, drafting boys and old men; at Acosta Ñu in 1869 children fought the Brazilian army, a battle Paraguay remembers on its Children’s Day. He was killed at Cerro Corá in 1870. Estimates of Paraguay’s losses range from about a quarter to more than half of its people, with adult men suffering most.
story.zh:
索拉诺·洛佩斯继承了一个中央集权国家，拥有或达六七万人的军队，为该地区之最。1864年巴西干预乌拉圭内战，他扣押一艘巴西轮船并入侵马托格罗索；阿根廷拒绝让其军队借道科连特斯，因而卷入战争。1865年5月1日签订的《三国同盟条约》规定盟国须战至洛佩斯下台为止。

战事在扼守巴拉圭河的乌迈塔要塞周围陷入僵局。1866年9月在库鲁派蒂，盟军正面强攻损失数千人，霍乱也在双方军中肆虐。承担主要战争负担的巴西于1868年派新式铁甲舰闯过乌迈塔。

洛佩斯退入内地，征召少年和老人入伍；1869年在阿科斯塔纽，儿童与巴西军队作战，巴拉圭以此日为儿童节。1870年他在塞罗科拉阵亡。对巴拉圭人口损失的估计从约四分之一到一半以上不等，成年男子损失最为惨重。

sources.title: Britannica: War of the Triple Alliance
Thomas L. Whigham, The Paraguayan War, vol. 1: Causes and Early Conduct (University of Nebraska Press, 2002)
Francisco Doratioto, Maldita guerra: nova história da Guerra do Paraguai (Companhia das Letras, 2002)

note: Population losses are disputed; see Whigham & Potthast, Latin American Research Review 34 (1999).

summary.en: A dispute over a Bolivian tax on a Chilean nitrate company led Chile to occupy Antofagasta in February 1879 and go to war with Bolivia and its ally Peru. Chile won command of the sea, conquered the nitrate provinces and occupied Lima; Bolivia lost its coast and Peru the province of Tarapacá.
summary.zh: 因玻利维亚对一家智利硝石公司征税引发争端，智利于1879年2月占领安托法加斯塔，与玻利维亚及其盟国秘鲁开战。智利夺得制海权，征服硝石产区并占领利马；玻利维亚失去出海口，秘鲁失去塔拉帕卡省。

强攻阿里卡（6月7日）
乔里约斯与米拉弗洛雷斯之战（1月）

《安孔条约》

story.en:
The Atacama desert held the world’s richest deposits of nitrate, prized as fertiliser and for explosives. Chilean capital and workers dominated the industry even in the Bolivian province of Antofagasta, and when Bolivia raised a tax of ten centavos per hundredweight in breach of an 1874 treaty and threatened to seize the company, Chile sent troops.

Peru, bound to Bolivia by a secret alliance, was drawn in. At Iquique on 21 May 1879 the Peruvian ironclad Huáscar under Miguel Grau sank the old Chilean corvette Esmeralda, whose captain Arturo Prat died leaping onto the enemy’s deck; both men became national heroes. In October the Chilean navy cornered and captured the Huáscar off Angamos, killing Grau.

With the sea secured, Chile took Tarapacá, Tacna and Arica, and in January 1881 entered Lima. Peruvian resistance under Andrés Cáceres continued in the highlands until the Treaty of Ancón in 1883. Bolivia has demanded access to the sea ever since.
story.zh:
阿塔卡马沙漠蕴藏着世界上最丰富的硝石矿，硝石既是珍贵的肥料，也是炸药原料。即使在玻利维亚的安托法加斯塔省，这一产业也由智利资本和工人主导。玻利维亚违反1874年条约，对每英担征税十分并威胁没收公司，智利随即出兵。

与玻利维亚订有秘密同盟的秘鲁被卷入战争。1879年5月21日在伊基克，米格尔·格劳指挥的秘鲁铁甲舰“瓦斯卡尔”号击沉了智利老式轻巡洋舰“埃斯梅拉达”号，舰长阿图罗·普拉特跃上敌舰甲板时牺牲，两人都成为民族英雄。10月，智利海军在安加莫斯外海围住并俘获“瓦斯卡尔”号，格劳阵亡。

掌握制海权后，智利夺取塔拉帕卡、塔克纳和阿里卡，1881年1月进入利马。秘鲁人在安德烈斯·卡塞雷斯领导下在高原继续抵抗，直到1883年签订《安孔条约》。此后玻利维亚一直要求获得出海口。

sources.title: Britannica: War of the Pacific
William F. Sater, Andean Tragedy: Fighting the War of the Pacific, 1879–1884 (University of Nebraska Press, 2007)
Bruce W. Farcau, The Ten Cents War (Praeger, 2000)

summary.en: Argentine armies under Julio A. Roca, equipped with Remington rifles and the telegraph, swept the pampas and northern Patagonia, defeating the Mapuche, Ranquel and Tehuelche peoples. Thousands were killed or deported, and some 15 million hectares were opened to ranching and distributed to a few landowners.
summary.zh: 胡利奥·阿亨蒂诺·罗卡率领装备雷明顿步枪和电报的阿根廷军队横扫潘帕斯草原和巴塔哥尼亚北部，击败马普切人、兰克尔人和特维尔切人。数千人被杀或被迁徙，约1500万公顷土地被开辟为牧场，分配给少数地主。

story.en:
For centuries Indigenous confederations of the pampas had raided frontier ranches for cattle, which they traded across the Andes to Chile. In 1879 Roca, then minister of war, launched a coordinated offensive with five divisions converging on the Río Negro, which his army reached at Choele Choel on 25 May.

Campaigns continued until the last great leader, Valentín Sayhueque, surrendered in 1885. Captured families were separated and sent to work on sugar estates in Tucumán, as domestic servants in Buenos Aires or to the island of Martín García.

The campaign made Roca president in 1880 and turned Patagonia into sheep country. In recent decades Argentine historians and Mapuche organisations have called it a genocide, and statues of Roca have become the focus of protests.
story.zh:
数百年来，潘帕斯草原的原住民联盟不时袭击边境牧场掠夺牛群，再翻越安第斯山卖到智利。1879年，时任陆军部长的罗卡发动协同攻势，五个师向内格罗河会师，5月25日其军队抵达乔埃莱乔埃尔。

战事持续到1885年最后一位大首领巴伦廷·赛韦克投降为止。被俘家庭被拆散，被送往图库曼的甘蔗庄园做工、到布宜诺斯艾利斯当仆役，或押往马丁·加西亚岛。

这场战役使罗卡于1880年当选总统，并把巴塔哥尼亚变成牧羊之地。近几十年来，阿根廷史学家和马普切组织称之为种族灭绝，罗卡的雕像也成为抗议的焦点。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Conquest of the Desert
David Rock, Argentina 1516–1987 (University of California Press, 1987)
Walter Delrio, Memorias de expropiación: sometimiento e incorporación indígena en la Patagonia, 1872–1943 (UNQ, 2005)

note: Roca’s troops reached the Río Negro on 25 May 1879.

summary.en: After centuries of Mapuche independence south of the Biobío, the Chilean state advanced a line of forts into Araucanía, crushed a last great uprising in 1881 and refounded Villarrica in 1883. Mapuche land was confined to small reservations and opened to Chilean and European settlers.
summary.zh: 在比奥比奥河以南的马普切人独立数百年之后，智利国家把一道要塞线推进到阿劳卡尼亚，1881年镇压了最后一次大起义，1883年重建比亚里卡。马普切人的土地被压缩为小块保留地，其余向智利和欧洲移民开放。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Occupation of Araucanía
José Bengoa, Historia del pueblo mapuche (Ediciones Sur, 1985)

summary.en: Demand for rubber for bicycle and car tyres made wild Amazonian latex one of the world’s most valuable commodities. Manaus and Belém grew opulent on the trade, while tappers bound by debt, many of them drought refugees from Ceará, and enslaved Indigenous people in the Putumayo paid a terrible price.
summary.zh: 自行车和汽车轮胎对橡胶的需求使亚马孙野生乳胶成为世界上最值钱的商品之一。马瑙斯和贝伦因贸易而奢华，而受债务束缚的割胶工（许多是塞阿拉州的旱灾难民）以及普图马约被奴役的原住民则付出了惨痛代价。

story.en:
Vulcanisation, patented in the 1840s, and the pneumatic tyre of the 1880s turned latex from the Hevea tree into an industrial necessity. Hundreds of thousands of migrants went up the Amazon’s tributaries to tap scattered trees, advanced food and tools by traders under the aviamento system and rarely able to escape their debts.

Manaus built the Teatro Amazonas, opened in 1896 with Italian marble and French ironwork, electric streetlights and trams. Brazil also fought Bolivia for the rubber-rich Acre, which it acquired by the Treaty of Petrópolis in 1903. On the Putumayo, the Peruvian Amazon Company of Julio César Arana enslaved Uitoto and other peoples; the British consul Roger Casement’s report of 1912 documented thousands of deaths.

In 1876 the Englishman Henry Wickham had shipped some 70,000 rubber seeds to Kew Gardens, and plantations in British Malaya and Ceylon soon produced cheaper rubber. By 1913 Asian output exceeded Amazonian, and the boom collapsed almost overnight.
story.zh:
19世纪40年代获得专利的硫化技术和80年代的充气轮胎，使橡胶树乳胶成为工业必需品。数十万移民沿亚马孙支流而上，采割分散的橡胶树；他们在“预付制”下从商人那里赊取食物和工具，很少能摆脱债务。

马瑙斯修建了1896年落成的亚马孙剧院，用上了意大利大理石和法国铁艺，还有电灯和电车。巴西还与玻利维亚争夺盛产橡胶的阿克里，并于1903年通过《彼得罗波利斯条约》将其收入版图。在普图马约河流域，胡利奥·塞萨尔·阿拉纳的秘鲁亚马孙公司奴役维托托人等民族；英国领事罗杰·凯斯门特1912年的报告记录了数以千计的死亡。

1876年英国人亨利·威克姆把约七万颗橡胶种子运到邱园，英属马来亚和锡兰的种植园很快生产出更廉价的橡胶。到1913年亚洲产量超过亚马孙，繁荣几乎在一夜之间崩溃。

sources.title: Barbara Weinstein, The Amazon Rubber Boom, 1850–1920 (Stanford UP, 1983)
Roger Casement, Correspondence Respecting the Treatment of British Colonial Subjects and Native Indians Employed in the Collection of Rubber in the Putumayo District (HMSO, 1912)
Wikipedia: Amazon rubber cycle

note: The boom is variously dated from the 1850s or 1879 to its collapse in 1912–13.

name.en: Golden Law abolishes slavery in Brazil

summary.en: On 13 May 1888 Princess Isabel, as regent, signed a two-article law ending slavery in Brazil without compensation to owners. About 700,000 people were freed. Brazil, which had received more enslaved Africans than any other country, was the last nation in the Americas to abolish slavery.
summary.zh: 1888年5月13日，摄政的伊莎贝尔公主签署了一部仅有两条的法律，废除巴西奴隶制，且不对奴隶主作任何补偿，约70万人获得自由。巴西接收的被奴役非洲人多于任何其他国家，也是美洲最后一个废除奴隶制的国家。

story.en:
Some 4.8 million enslaved Africans were landed in Brazil over three centuries, about four in ten of all those carried across the Atlantic. Under British pressure the trade was effectively ended in 1850; the Law of Free Birth of 1871 freed children born to enslaved mothers, and an 1885 law freed those over sixty.

In the 1880s abolition became a mass movement. Joaquim Nabuco, André Rebouças and José do Patrocínio campaigned in parliament and the press, the province of Ceará freed its slaves in 1884, and in São Paulo enslaved people fled plantations in their thousands with the help of activists known as caifazes, while the army refused to hunt them down.

The final law, passed almost unanimously, read simply that slavery was declared extinct. Crowds celebrated in Rio for days. But no land or schooling was offered to the freed, and many planters turned against the monarchy, which fell eighteen months later.
story.zh:
三个世纪里约有480万被奴役的非洲人被运到巴西，约占跨大西洋贩运总数的十分之四。在英国压力下，奴隶贸易于1850年实际终止；1871年《自由出生法》使女奴所生子女获得自由，1885年的法律又解放了60岁以上的奴隶。

19世纪80年代废奴成为群众运动。若阿金·纳布科、安德烈·雷博萨斯和若泽·杜帕特罗西尼奥在议会和报刊上奔走呼号；塞阿拉省于1884年解放全部奴隶；在圣保罗，被奴役者在被称为“凯法塞斯”的活动人士帮助下成千上万地逃离种植园，而军队拒绝追捕他们。

这部几乎全票通过的最终法律只简单写道：奴隶制宣告废除。里约民众连续数日欢庆。然而获得自由的人没有分到土地，也没有受教育的机会；许多种植园主转而反对帝制，十八个月后君主制覆灭。

sources.title: Robert Edgar Conrad, The Destruction of Brazilian Slavery, 1850–1888 (University of California Press, 1972)
Emília Viotti da Costa, Da senzala à colônia (1966)
Wikipedia: Lei Áurea

note: The figure of 4.8 million embarkations follows the Trans-Atlantic Slave Trade Database (slavevoyages.org).

name.en: Proclamation of the Republic in Brazil

summary.en: On 15 November 1889 army officers under Marshal Deodoro da Fonseca, backed by republican politicians, deposed the cabinet in Rio and proclaimed a republic almost without bloodshed. Emperor Pedro II and his family were sent into exile in Europe two days later.
summary.zh: 1889年11月15日，德奥多罗·达丰塞卡元帅率领的军官在共和派政治家支持下，在里约推翻内阁，几乎未经流血便宣告成立共和国。两天后皇帝佩德罗二世及其家人被流放欧洲。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Proclamation of the Republic (Brazil)
Roderick J. Barman, Citizen Emperor: Pedro II and the Making of Brazil (1999)

summary.en: In the drought-stricken backlands of Bahia, the lay preacher Antônio Conselheiro gathered tens of thousands of poor followers at Canudos. The young republic saw a monarchist threat and sent four military expeditions; the last, with artillery, destroyed the town in October 1897 and killed most of its people.
summary.zh: 在饱受干旱的巴伊亚腹地，平信徒传道者安东尼奥·孔塞列罗在卡努杜斯聚集了数万贫苦信徒。年轻的共和国视之为君主派威胁，先后派出四支讨伐军；最后一支携带火炮，于1897年10月摧毁该镇，屠杀了大部分居民。

story.en:
Antônio Conselheiro, “the Counsellor”, wandered the sertão for decades rebuilding churches and cemeteries. In 1893 he settled on an abandoned ranch by the Vaza-Barris river, which he called Belo Monte. Landless farmers, freed slaves and Indigenous people flocked there, and within four years it was one of the largest towns in Bahia.

Its refusal to pay republican taxes and its preaching against civil marriage alarmed the authorities. Three expeditions were routed between 1896 and early 1897, the third losing its commander, Colonel Moreira César. A fourth army of several thousand men with heavy guns besieged the town for months; Conselheiro died in September, and the last defenders fell on 5 October 1897.

The journalist Euclides da Cunha followed the campaign and wrote Os Sertões (1902), a classic that exposed the massacre. Returning soldiers settled on a Rio hillside they named after the Favela hill at Canudos, giving Brazil the word for its hillside shantytowns.
story.zh:
“顾问”安东尼奥·孔塞列罗在腹地游历数十年，修缮教堂和墓地。1893年他在瓦萨巴里斯河畔一座废弃的牧场定居，称之为“美山”。无地农民、获释奴隶和原住民纷纷涌来，四年之内这里已成为巴伊亚最大的城镇之一。

该镇拒绝缴纳共和国的赋税、宣讲反对民事婚姻，令当局惊恐。1896年至1897年初，三支讨伐军相继溃败，第三支连指挥官莫雷拉·塞萨尔上校也战死。第四支数千人的大军携重炮围城数月；孔塞列罗于9月去世，最后的守卫者于1897年10月5日倒下。

记者欧克利德斯·达库尼亚随军采访，写成经典之作《腹地》（1902年），揭露了这场屠杀。复员士兵在里约一处山坡上定居，以卡努杜斯的“法维拉”山为之命名，巴西从此有了称呼山坡贫民窟的词语“favela”。

sources.title: Euclides da Cunha, Os Sertões (1902)
Robert M. Levine, Vale of Tears: Revisiting the Canudos Massacre in Northeastern Brazil, 1893–1897 (University of California Press, 1992)
Wikipedia: War of Canudos

note: Wikidata dates the conflict 1895–1898; the military campaigns ran from November 1896 to October 1897.

name.zh: 海勒姆·宾厄姆抵达马丘比丘

summary.en: Searching for Vilcabamba, the Yale lecturer Hiram Bingham was led up to Machu Picchu by the farmer Melchor Arteaga on 24 July 1911 and found local families living on its terraces. His photographs, published by National Geographic in 1913, made the site world-famous.
summary.zh: 为寻找比尔卡班巴，耶鲁讲师海勒姆·宾厄姆于1911年7月24日由农民梅尔乔·阿特亚加带上马丘比丘，发现当地家庭正在其梯田上耕种。1913年《国家地理》发表了他的照片，使这一遗址闻名世界。

story.en:
Bingham set out from Cusco with a small Yale team to find the last Inca refuge described in the chronicles. At Mandor Pampa on the Urubamba, the innkeeper Melchor Arteaga told him of ruins on the mountain above. On a rainy morning Bingham, Arteaga and a police sergeant crawled across a log bridge and climbed the slope, where the farmers Richarte and Álvarez sent a boy to show them the stonework.

Bingham was not the first outsider there: a farmer, Agustín Lizárraga, had written his name in charcoal on a wall in 1902. But he was the first to recognise its importance and publicise it. He returned in 1912 with National Geographic backing, cleared the vegetation and shipped thousands of artefacts to Yale.

Bingham believed he had found Vilcabamba; it was in fact at Espíritu Pampa, which he had also visited. After a long dispute, Yale returned the collections to Peru in 2011–12, where they are kept in Cusco.
story.zh:
宾厄姆率领一支耶鲁小分队从库斯科出发，寻找编年史所述的最后一个印加避难所。在乌鲁班巴河畔的曼多尔潘帕，客栈主人梅尔乔·阿特亚加告诉他山上有遗迹。一个雨天的早晨，宾厄姆、阿特亚加和一名警官爬过一座圆木桥攀上山坡，在那里耕种的农民里查尔特和阿尔瓦雷斯派一个男孩带他们去看石造建筑。

宾厄姆并非第一个到达这里的外人：农民阿古斯丁·利萨拉加早在1902年就用木炭在墙上写下了自己的名字。但宾厄姆是第一个认识到其重要性并公之于世的人。1912年他在《国家地理》资助下重返，清除植被，并把数千件文物运往耶鲁。

宾厄姆以为自己找到了比尔卡班巴，而真正的比尔卡班巴在他也曾到过的埃斯皮里图潘帕。经过长期争执，耶鲁于2011至2012年把藏品归还秘鲁，现保存于库斯科。

sources.title: Hiram Bingham, “In the Wonderland of Peru”, National Geographic Magazine 24:4 (April 1913)
Christopher Heaney, Cradle of Gold: The Story of Hiram Bingham (Palgrave Macmillan, 2010)
Britannica: Machu Picchu

name.en: Modern Art Week in São Paulo

summary.en: In February 1922, the centenary year of independence, young artists, writers and musicians staged three nights of exhibitions, readings and concerts at the Theatro Municipal of São Paulo. Booed by much of the audience, the Week launched Brazilian modernism and its search for a national art.
summary.zh: 1922年2月，正值独立百年，一批年轻的艺术家、作家和音乐家在圣保罗市立剧院举办了三晚展览、朗诵和音乐会。尽管遭到大部分观众嘘声，“艺术周”开启了巴西现代主义及其对民族艺术的探索。

story.en:
The organisers, among them the poets Mário de Andrade and Oswald de Andrade and the painters Anita Malfatti and Di Cavalcanti, wanted to shake Brazilian culture free of academic imitation of Europe. Coffee money from São Paulo’s elite paid for the event.

On the second night Mário de Andrade read from the steps while the audience jeered and imitated animal noises. The composer Heitor Villa-Lobos appeared with one shoe and one slipper; the crowd took it as provocation, though he was nursing a sore foot.

The Week’s ideas bore fruit later in the decade: Tarsila do Amaral painted Abaporu in 1928, and Oswald’s Anthropophagic Manifesto of the same year proposed that Brazil should “devour” foreign culture and turn it into something new.
story.zh:
组织者包括诗人马里奥·德·安德拉德和奥斯瓦尔德·德·安德拉德、画家阿妮塔·马尔法蒂和迪·卡瓦尔坎蒂，他们希望使巴西文化摆脱对欧洲学院派的模仿。活动经费来自圣保罗精英阶层的咖啡财富。

第二晚，马里奥·德·安德拉德站在台阶上朗诵，观众起哄喝倒彩、学动物叫。作曲家埃托尔·维拉-罗伯斯一只脚穿鞋、一只脚穿拖鞋登台，观众以为这是挑衅，其实他是脚疼。

艺术周的理念在十年后期开花结果：塔尔西拉·多·阿马拉尔于1928年画出《阿巴波鲁》，同年奥斯瓦尔德发表《食人宣言》，主张巴西应“吞食”外来文化，再将其转化为新的东西。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Modern Art Week
Aracy Amaral, Artes plásticas na Semana de 22 (Perspectiva, 1970)
MoMA, Tarsila do Amaral: Inventing Modern Art in Brazil (exhibition catalogue, 2018)

summary.en: After the disputed election of 1930 and the murder of his running mate João Pessoa, Getúlio Vargas led an uprising from Rio Grande do Sul, Minas Gerais and Paraíba. Within a month the army deposed President Washington Luís, ending the Old Republic and opening fifteen years of Vargas rule.
summary.zh: 1930年选举结果引发争议、其竞选伙伴若昂·佩索阿遇刺后，热图利奥·瓦加斯在南里奥格兰德、米纳斯吉拉斯和帕拉伊巴发动起义。一个月内军队推翻总统华盛顿·路易斯，结束了旧共和国，开启瓦加斯长达十五年的统治。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Brazilian Revolution of 1930
Boris Fausto, A Revolução de 1930 (Brasiliense, 1970)

summary.en: The 30 m statue of Christ with outstretched arms, designed by Heitor da Silva Costa with the French sculptor Paul Landowski and clad in a mosaic of soapstone tiles, was inaugurated on the summit of Corcovado on 12 October 1931. It became the emblem of Rio and of Brazil.
summary.zh: 这尊高30米、双臂张开的基督像由埃托尔·达席尔瓦·科斯塔与法国雕塑家保罗·兰多夫斯基设计，外覆皂石马赛克，于1931年10月12日在科尔科瓦多山顶落成，成为里约和巴西的象征。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Christ the Redeemer (statue)
UNESCO World Heritage: Rio de Janeiro: Carioca Landscapes between the Mountain and the Sea

summary.en: Bolivia and Paraguay fought for the arid Gran Chaco, which both claimed and where oil was suspected. Despite Bolivia’s larger population and German-trained army, Paraguay’s troops, at home in the scrub, won most battles. Some 90,000–100,000 men died, many of thirst and disease.
summary.zh: 玻利维亚与巴拉圭为双方都声称拥有、且被怀疑蕴藏石油的干旱大查科地区而战。尽管玻利维亚人口更多、军队由德国人训练，熟悉灌木丛林的巴拉圭军队赢得了大多数战役。约9万至10万人死亡，许多人死于干渴和疾病。

story.en:
Bolivia, having lost its Pacific coast, hoped to reach the Paraguay river through the Chaco. Rumours that Standard Oil and Royal Dutch Shell stood behind the two sides were widespread, though historians now give them less weight. Small forts had been pushed into the scrubland for years before a clash over the lake fort of Pitiantuta in June 1932 escalated into war; the first great battle was fought at Boquerón that September.

Paraguay mobilised nearly its whole male population under Colonel José Félix Estigarribia, who used encirclements and knowledge of the waterholes. Highland Bolivian conscripts, many of them Aymara and Quechua peasants, suffered terribly from heat and lack of water.

A truce in June 1935 and the treaty of 1938 gave Paraguay most of the disputed land. In Bolivia, veterans’ anger at the war helped spark the 1952 National Revolution.
story.zh:
失去太平洋海岸的玻利维亚希望经查科地区通达巴拉圭河。当时盛传标准石油公司和荷兰皇家壳牌分别是双方的幕后推手，不过史学家如今已不太看重这一说法。双方多年来不断向灌木荒原推进小型堡垒，1932年6月围绕皮蒂安图塔湖畔堡垒的冲突升级为战争，同年9月在博克龙爆发了第一场大战。

巴拉圭在何塞·费利克斯·埃斯蒂加里维亚上校指挥下几乎动员了全部男性人口，他善用包围战术并熟知水源分布。来自高原的玻利维亚新兵多为艾马拉和克丘亚农民，饱受酷热和缺水之苦。

1935年6月停火，1938年条约将大部分争议土地划归巴拉圭。在玻利维亚，老兵们对战争的愤怒促成了1952年的国民革命。

sources.title: Britannica: Chaco War
Bruce W. Farcau, The Chaco War: Bolivia and Paraguay, 1932–1935 (Praeger, 1996)
Herbert S. Klein, A Concise History of Bolivia (Cambridge UP, 2003)

summary.en: After rivals in the military government forced Colonel Juan Perón to resign and arrested him, tens of thousands of workers from the industrial suburbs marched into the Plaza de Mayo. That night Perón was freed and spoke from the balcony of the Casa Rosada, a day Peronists still celebrate as Loyalty Day.
summary.zh: 军政府中的对手迫使胡安·庇隆上校辞职并将其逮捕后，数以万计的工人从工业郊区涌入五月广场。当晚庇隆获释，并在玫瑰宫阳台上发表讲话，庇隆主义者至今以此日为“忠诚日”。

story.en:
As secretary of labour from 1943, Perón had raised wages, backed unions and given rural workers new rights, making enemies among employers and fellow officers. On 9 October 1945 he was forced out of his posts and soon taken to the island of Martín García.

On 17 October workers from Berisso, Avellaneda and other industrial towns crossed the Riachuelo, some swimming when the bridges were raised, and filled the Plaza de Mayo. Middle-class Buenos Aires was shocked to see them cooling their feet in the square’s fountains.

Near midnight Perón appeared on the balcony. He married Eva Duarte days later and won the presidential election of February 1946. Popular memory gave Evita a leading role in organising the march, but historians find little evidence of it.
story.zh:
1943年起任劳工部长的庇隆提高工资、支持工会、赋予农村工人新的权利，因而在雇主和军官同僚中树敌。1945年10月9日他被迫辞去职务，不久被押往马丁·加西亚岛。

10月17日，来自贝里索、阿韦利亚内达等工业城镇的工人渡过里亚丘埃洛河——吊桥升起时有人干脆游过去——挤满了五月广场。布宜诺斯艾利斯的中产阶级震惊地看到他们在广场喷泉里泡脚纳凉。

临近午夜，庇隆出现在阳台上。几天后他与伊娃·杜阿尔特结婚，并在1946年2月的总统选举中获胜。民间记忆认为艾薇塔在组织游行中起了主导作用，但史学家几乎找不到相关证据。

sources.title: Daniel James, Resistance and Integration: Peronism and the Argentine Working Class, 1946–1976 (Cambridge UP, 1988)
Joseph A. Page, Perón: A Biography (1983)
Wikipedia: Loyalty Day (Argentina)

name.zh: “马拉卡纳之殇”：乌拉圭击败巴西

summary.en: In the deciding match of the 1950 World Cup, before about 200,000 spectators in Rio’s new Maracanã stadium, Uruguay came from behind to beat the host nation 2–1. The defeat became a national trauma in Brazil and a founding legend of Uruguayan football.
summary.zh: 在1950年世界杯的决胜场比赛中，约20万观众挤满里约新建的马拉卡纳体育场，乌拉圭逆转以2比1击败东道主。这场失利成为巴西的民族创伤，也成为乌拉圭足球的奠基传奇。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Uruguay v Brazil (1950 FIFA World Cup)
Alex Bellos, Futebol: The Brazilian Way of Life (Bloomsbury, 2002)

summary.en: João Gilberto’s 1958 recording of “Chega de Saudade” by Antônio Carlos Jobim and Vinicius de Moraes, with its whispered voice and syncopated guitar, launched bossa nova in Rio’s southern beach districts. “The Girl from Ipanema” (1962) carried it around the world.
summary.zh: 1958年，若昂·吉尔贝托录制了安东尼奥·卡洛斯·若比姆与维尼修斯·德莫赖斯创作的《不再忧伤》，以低吟的嗓音和切分的吉他声在里约南区海滨开创了波萨诺瓦。《来自伊帕内玛的女孩》（1962年）使其风靡全球。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Bossa nova
Ruy Castro, Chega de Saudade: The Story of Bossa Nova (1990; English ed. A Cappella, 2000)

name.zh: 智利大地震（瓦尔迪维亚地震）

summary.en: On 22 May 1960 a magnitude 9.5 earthquake, the most powerful ever recorded, ruptured about 1,000 km of the fault off southern Chile. It devastated Valdivia and surrounding towns, raised a Pacific-wide tsunami that killed people in Hawaii, Japan and the Philippines, and dammed Lake Riñihue.
summary.zh: 1960年5月22日，一场9.5级地震——有记录以来最强烈的地震——使智利南部外海约1000公里长的断层破裂。地震摧毁了瓦尔迪维亚及周边城镇，引发横扫太平洋的海啸，在夏威夷、日本和菲律宾造成伤亡，并堵塞了里尼韦湖。

story.en:
A day earlier a magnitude 8 foreshock had shaken Concepción. The main shock struck in mid-afternoon and lasted around ten minutes. Coastal land sank by up to two metres, turning fields into marshes, and tsunami waves up to 25 metres high swept the coast; deaths in Chile are estimated at between 1,000 and 2,000.

Fifteen hours later the tsunami struck Hilo in Hawaii, killing 61 people, and after 22 hours it reached Japan, where some 140 died. Two days after the quake the Cordón Caulle volcano erupted.

The greatest danger came from the Riñihuazo: landslides had blocked the outlet of Lake Riñihue, and the rising water threatened to burst through and flood Valdivia. For two months engineers of the state power company and hundreds of workers dug channels by hand and machine to drain the lake slowly, saving the city.
story.zh:
前一天，一场8级前震震撼了康塞普西翁。主震发生在午后，持续约十分钟。沿海陆地下沉多达两米，田野变成沼泽，高达25米的海啸巨浪席卷海岸；智利国内死亡人数估计在1000至2000人之间。

15小时后海啸袭击夏威夷希洛，造成61人死亡；22小时后抵达日本，约140人遇难。地震两天后，科尔东考列火山喷发。

最大的危险来自“里尼韦湖堵塞事件”：山体滑坡堵住了里尼韦湖的出口，上涨的湖水随时可能溃决、淹没瓦尔迪维亚。国家电力公司的工程师和数百名工人用了两个月，以人力和机械开挖水渠，使湖水缓慢泄出，挽救了这座城市。

sources.title: USGS, M 9.5 – 1960 Great Chilean Earthquake (Valdivia Earthquake)
Wikipedia: 1960 Valdivia earthquake
Pierre St-Amand, “Los terremotos de mayo – Chile 1960”, Michelson Laboratories Technical Article 14 (1961)

note: Death toll estimates range from about 1,000 to 6,000; 1,655 is a widely cited figure.

summary.en: President Juscelino Kubitschek fulfilled a constitutional promise of 1891 by building a new capital on the empty central plateau in under four years. Lúcio Costa’s Pilot Plan, shaped like a bird or aeroplane, and Oscar Niemeyer’s white modernist palaces were inaugurated on 21 April 1960.
summary.zh: 儒塞利诺·库比契克总统兑现了1891年宪法的承诺，用不到四年时间在空旷的中部高原上建起新首都。卢西奥·科斯塔设计的形如飞鸟或飞机的“试点规划”和奥斯卡·尼迈耶的白色现代主义宫殿于1960年4月21日落成启用。

story.en:
Kubitschek campaigned in 1955 on “fifty years of progress in five”, and Brasília was his showpiece, meant to pull development into the interior. Costa won the planning competition of 1957 with a few freehand sketches: two crossing axes, one monumental with the ministries and the Three Powers Square, one curving with residential superblocks.

Tens of thousands of workers, the candangos, many from the poor north-east, built the city in about 41 months, with materials flown in before roads were finished. Niemeyer’s National Congress, with its twin towers and paired domes, and his crown-shaped cathedral became icons of modern architecture.

Critics noted that the workers were pushed out to satellite towns the plan had not foreseen. Brasília was declared a World Heritage site in 1987 and now has a metropolitan population of more than four million.
story.zh:
库比契克在1955年竞选时提出“五年实现五十年的进步”，巴西利亚是他的标志性工程，意在把发展引向内陆。科斯塔在1957年的规划竞赛中凭几幅徒手草图胜出：两条交叉的轴线，一条是排列着各部大楼和三权广场的纪念轴，另一条弯曲的轴线上是住宅超级街区。

数以万计的工人——被称为“坎丹戈”，许多来自贫困的东北部——用约41个月建成了这座城市，道路尚未修通时建材靠飞机运入。尼迈耶设计的国会大厦（双塔与一仰一覆的双穹顶）和王冠形的大教堂成为现代建筑的象征。

批评者指出，工人被推到了规划未曾预见的卫星城中。1987年巴西利亚被列为世界遗产，如今都市区人口已超过四百万。

sources.title: UNESCO World Heritage: Brasilia
James Holston, The Modernist City: An Anthropological Critique of Brasília (University of Chicago Press, 1989)
Britannica: Brasília

name.en: One Hundred Years of Solitude published

summary.en: Gabriel García Márquez’s saga of seven generations of the Buendía family in the imaginary town of Macondo was published by Editorial Sudamericana in Buenos Aires in May 1967. It became the emblem of magical realism and the Latin American Boom, selling tens of millions of copies.
summary.zh: 加夫列尔·加西亚·马尔克斯讲述虚构小镇马孔多布恩迪亚家族七代人的史诗，于1967年5月由布宜诺斯艾利斯的南美出版社出版。它成为魔幻现实主义和拉丁美洲“文学爆炸”的象征，销量达数千万册。

story.en:
García Márquez had carried the idea for nearly twenty years when, driving to Acapulco in 1965, he suddenly saw how to tell it: in the deadpan voice his grandmother used for marvels. He shut himself away in Mexico City for some eighteen months while his wife Mercedes kept the family on credit and pawned household goods.

According to his own account, when he went to post the manuscript to Buenos Aires they could afford to send only half, and he discovered later that he had sent the second half first. The first printing of 8,000 copies sold out within weeks.

Macondo drew on Aracataca and on the banana-zone massacre of 1928. The novel helped win him the Nobel Prize in 1982, and a Colombian-made television series of it appeared in 2024.
story.zh:
加西亚·马尔克斯酝酿这个构思近二十年，1965年驾车前往阿卡普尔科途中，他突然找到了讲述的方式：用外祖母讲述奇事时那种不动声色的口吻。他在墨西哥城闭门写作约十八个月，妻子梅塞德斯靠赊账和典当家当维持全家生计。

据他本人讲述，去邮局把书稿寄往布宜诺斯艾利斯时，钱只够寄一半，后来他才发现先寄出去的是后半部分。首印8000册在几周内售罄。

马孔多取材于阿拉卡塔卡和1928年香蕉种植区大屠杀。这部小说助他赢得1982年诺贝尔奖，2024年哥伦比亚还拍摄了同名电视剧。

sources.title: Gerald Martin, Gabriel García Márquez: A Life (Bloomsbury, 2008)
Gabriel García Márquez, Vivir para contarla (2002)
Wikipedia: One Hundred Years of Solitude

summary.en: On 11 September 1973 the armed forces under General Augusto Pinochet overthrew President Salvador Allende. Air force jets bombed La Moneda palace, where Allende died; the junta that followed ruled for 17 years, during which more than 3,000 people were killed or disappeared and tens of thousands were tortured.
summary.zh: 1973年9月11日，奥古斯托·皮诺切特将军领导的武装部队推翻萨尔瓦多·阿连德总统。空军战机轰炸拉莫内达宫，阿连德死于宫中；此后军政府统治17年，3000多人被杀或失踪，数以万计的人遭受酷刑。

story.en:
Allende’s Popular Unity government had nationalised copper, accelerated land reform and taken over banks and factories, while inflation soared, shortages spread and the opposition and much of the middle class turned against it. The United States, which saw a Marxist government as a threat, funded opponents through the CIA.

At dawn on 11 September the navy seized Valparaíso. Allende went to La Moneda with a few guards and advisers, refused offers of safe passage and spoke a last time on Radio Magallanes, saying he would pay with his life for the people’s loyalty. Hawker Hunter jets rocketed the palace shortly before noon, and he took his own life as troops entered, as a judicial exhumation confirmed in 2011.

The National Stadium became a detention camp, the singer Víctor Jara was murdered and Neruda died twelve days later. The truth commissions of 1991 and 2004 documented the dictatorship’s killings and torture.
story.zh:
阿连德的人民团结政府将铜矿国有化、加快土地改革并接管银行和工厂，与此同时通货膨胀飙升、物资短缺蔓延，反对派和大部分中产阶级转而反对政府。视马克思主义政府为威胁的美国通过中央情报局资助反对派。

9月11日黎明，海军占领瓦尔帕莱索。阿连德带着少数卫兵和顾问前往拉莫内达宫，拒绝了安全离开的提议，最后一次通过麦哲伦电台讲话，表示将以生命回报人民的忠诚。中午前不久，“猎人”式战机向总统府发射火箭；军队攻入时他开枪自尽，2011年的司法开棺检验证实了这一点。

国家体育场变成了拘押营，歌手维克托·哈拉遇害，聂鲁达在十二天后去世。1991年和2004年的真相委员会记录了独裁政权的杀戮和酷刑。

sources.title: Britannica: Salvador Allende
Peter Kornbluh, The Pinochet File (New Press, 2003)
Comisión Nacional de Verdad y Reconciliación (Rettig Report), Informe (1991)

name.en: Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo begin their marches
name.zh: 五月广场母亲开始游行

summary.en: On 30 April 1977 fourteen women whose children had been abducted by Argentina’s military regime gathered in the Plaza de Mayo to demand news of them. Forbidden to stand together, they walked in circles around the square every Thursday, their white headscarves becoming a worldwide symbol of the search for the disappeared.
summary.zh: 1977年4月30日，十四位子女被阿根廷军政府绑架的妇女聚集在五月广场，要求得知孩子的下落。由于不准聚集站立，她们每周四绕着广场转圈行走，她们的白头巾成为全世界寻找失踪者的象征。

story.en:
After the coup of March 1976, Argentina’s junta waged a “Dirty War” against leftists, unionists, students and anyone suspected of subversion. Thousands were seized by plainclothes squads, tortured in secret detention centres such as the Navy Mechanics School, and killed, many thrown alive from aircraft into the River Plate.

Azucena Villaflor, whose son had disappeared, proposed going to the Plaza de Mayo, in front of the Casa Rosada. When police ordered them to move along, the mothers began to walk arm in arm around the central pyramid. In December 1977 Villaflor and two French nuns were abducted after a naval officer, Alfredo Astiz, infiltrated the group; her remains were identified only in 2005.

The Mothers and the Grandmothers of the Plaza de Mayo kept marching through the dictatorship and after. The Grandmothers have helped identify more than 130 people who were stolen as babies from their imprisoned parents.
story.zh:
1976年3月政变后，阿根廷军政府对左派、工会成员、学生以及一切被怀疑颠覆的人发动“肮脏战争”。成千上万人被便衣行动队抓走，在海军机械学校等秘密拘押中心遭受酷刑并被杀害，许多人被从飞机上活活抛入拉普拉塔河。

儿子失踪的阿苏塞娜·维利亚弗洛尔提议到玫瑰宫前的五月广场去。警察命令她们离开时，母亲们便挽着手臂绕中央方尖碑行走。1977年12月，海军军官阿尔弗雷多·阿斯蒂斯混入团体后，维利亚弗洛尔和两名法国修女被绑架；她的遗骸直到2005年才得到确认。

五月广场母亲和五月广场祖母们在独裁期间及之后坚持游行。祖母们已帮助找回130多名在婴儿时期被从被囚父母身边偷走的人。

sources.title: Wikipedia: Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo
CONADEP, Nunca Más (1984)
Marguerite Guzman Bouvard, Revolutionizing Motherhood: The Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo (SR Books, 1994)

note: CONADEP documented about 9,000 disappearances; human-rights organisations estimate up to 30,000.

summary.en: Argentina’s military junta invaded the British-held Falkland Islands on 2 April 1982 to assert its claim to the Malvinas. Britain sent a naval task force 13,000 km south; after ten weeks of fighting the Argentine garrison surrendered at Stanley on 14 June. The defeat brought down the junta.
summary.zh: 1982年4月2日，阿根廷军政府入侵英国控制的福克兰群岛，以伸张其对马尔维纳斯群岛的主权。英国派遣海军特混舰队南下13000公里；经过十周战斗，阿根廷守军于6月14日在斯坦利投降。战败导致军政府垮台。

label.zh: 阿根廷军在斯坦利登陆（4月2日）
英军收复南乔治亚岛（4月25日）
“贝尔格拉诺将军”号巡洋舰被击沉（5月2日）

label.en: British landings at San Carlos (21 May)
label.zh: 英军在圣卡洛斯登陆（5月21日）
鹅原之战（5月28日）
阿根廷军在斯坦利投降（6月14日）

story.en:
Argentina had claimed the islands since Britain occupied them in 1833. In 1982 General Leopoldo Galtieri’s junta, facing economic crisis and growing protests, expected that Britain would not fight for 1,800 islanders so far away. Argentine marines took Stanley on 2 April, to celebration in Buenos Aires.

Margaret Thatcher’s government assembled a task force of carriers and requisitioned liners within days. On 2 May a British submarine sank the cruiser General Belgrano outside the exclusion zone, killing 323 men; two days later an Exocet missile fired by an Argentine aircraft destroyed HMS Sheffield. Argentine pilots sank several more ships during the landings at San Carlos.

British troops marched across East Falkland and took the hills around Stanley in night battles. In all 649 Argentines, 255 Britons and three islanders died. Galtieri fell within days, and democracy returned to Argentina in 1983; it still claims the islands.
story.zh:
自1833年英国占领群岛以来，阿根廷一直对其提出主权要求。1982年，面临经济危机和日益高涨的抗议，莱奥波尔多·加尔铁里将军的军政府认为英国不会为远在天边的1800名岛民开战。4月2日阿根廷海军陆战队占领斯坦利，布宜诺斯艾利斯一片欢腾。

玛格丽特·撒切尔政府几天之内就组建了一支包括航空母舰和征用邮轮的特混舰队。5月2日，一艘英国潜艇在禁区外击沉“贝尔格拉诺将军”号巡洋舰，323人丧生；两天后，阿根廷战机发射的“飞鱼”导弹击毁英舰“谢菲尔德”号。英军在圣卡洛斯登陆期间，阿根廷飞行员又击沉了数艘舰船。

英军徒步穿越东福克兰岛，在夜战中攻占斯坦利周围的山地。战争共造成649名阿根廷人、255名英国人和3名岛民死亡。加尔铁里在几天内下台，阿根廷于1983年恢复民主，至今仍主张对群岛的主权。

sources.title: Britannica: Falkland Islands War
Lawrence Freedman, The Official History of the Falklands Campaign (Routledge, 2005)
Max Hastings & Simon Jenkins, The Battle for the Falklands (Michael Joseph, 1983)

name.zh: 智利公投：对皮诺切特说“不”

summary.en: Under his own 1980 constitution, Pinochet asked voters to extend his rule for eight more years. A coalition of opposition parties ran a joyful television campaign under a rainbow logo, and “No” won about 56 per cent on 5 October 1988, opening the way to free elections in 1989.
summary.zh: 根据他本人制定的1980年宪法，皮诺切特要求选民同意将其统治再延长八年。反对派联盟以彩虹为标志开展了欢快的电视宣传，1988年10月5日“否”方赢得约56%的选票，为1989年自由选举铺平了道路。

name.en: Earth Summit in Rio de Janeiro

summary.en: The United Nations Conference on Environment and Development brought some 170 governments and more than 100 heads of state to Rio in June 1992. It opened for signature the Framework Convention on Climate Change and the Convention on Biological Diversity, and adopted Agenda 21.
summary.zh: 1992年6月，联合国环境与发展会议在里约召开，约170个国家政府和100多位国家元首与会。会议开放签署《联合国气候变化框架公约》和《生物多样性公约》，并通过了《21世纪议程》。

name.zh: 秘鲁内部冲突（光辉道路）

summary.en: The Maoist Shining Path began its war by burning ballot boxes in the Andean village of Chuschi in May 1980. Insurgent massacres and army repression devastated the highlands of Ayacucho until the capture of the leader Abimael Guzmán in 1992; Peru’s truth commission estimated about 69,000 deaths.
summary.zh: 毛主义组织“光辉道路”于1980年5月在安第斯山区的丘斯基村焚烧投票箱，开始了武装斗争。叛乱分子的屠杀和军队的镇压使阿亚库乔高原遭受重创，直到1992年其领导人阿维马埃尔·古斯曼被捕；秘鲁真相委员会估计约6.9万人死亡。

name.en: Rescue of the 33 miners at Copiapó

summary.en: A collapse at the San José copper and gold mine trapped 33 men 700 m underground. After 17 days a probe brought up their note “We are fine in the shelter, the 33”; on 13 October 2010, after 69 days, all were winched to the surface in the Fénix capsule, watched by a billion people.
summary.zh: 圣何塞铜金矿坍塌，33人被困地下700米。17天后，一根探钻带上来他们写的纸条：“我们33人在避难所里安好。”2010年10月13日，被困69天后，所有人乘“凤凰”号救生舱被逐一吊回地面，全球约十亿人观看了直播。

name.en: Colombian peace process with the FARC
name.zh: 哥伦比亚与哥伦比亚革命武装力量的和平进程

summary.en: After four years of talks in Havana, President Juan Manuel Santos and the FARC signed an agreement to end a 52-year conflict. Voters narrowly rejected it in October 2016; a revised text was signed in Bogotá in November and ratified by Congress, and Santos received the Nobel Peace Prize.
summary.zh: 经过在哈瓦那四年的谈判，胡安·曼努埃尔·桑托斯总统与哥伦比亚革命武装力量签署协议，结束长达52年的冲突。2016年10月选民以微弱多数否决协议；修订文本于11月在波哥大签署并获国会批准，桑托斯获诺贝尔和平奖。
